story.logline: A vigilante who falls in love with every unpunished man she sentences drives her latest across the desert, laughing and filming him, still waiting for the dead man to love her back.

beat_sheet.heading: COLD OPEN · EXT. EMPTY DESERT TOWN AND DESERT ROAD, OPEN TWO-SEATER – LATE AFTERNOON TO DUSK (0:00-0:56, V01)
beat_sheet.what_happens: VENUS wants to film JEAN looking back at her. JEAN, in all black, cheek on the headrest and head turned to the door, wants nothing: he is dead, and his stillness is the obstacle. Seen mostly inside her phone's upright frame, she drives him through an empty town and open desert, laughing hard enough to shake the picture. Tactic 1: she films him close, at arm's length. Tactic 2: at a stop sign nobody else will ever reach, she brushes the dust off his black shirt and straightens his collar. Tactic 3: her thumb moves to the flip-camera icon, then slides away. But the light is going. At dusk she lowers the phone, lifts off his sunglasses and turns his chin with two fingers. His eyes are open, pale and dusted, and they do not blink. She hooks one open arm of the sunglasses into her neckline, raises the phone, laughs, rests her thumb on the flip icon and slides it off again. Her flaw under pressure: she wants him to look at her, but she won't turn the lens on herself. Detail: she stops at a stop sign in an empty desert.
beat_sheet.turn: From a woman filming her sleeping lover to a woman filming a dead man she still won't step into frame with.

beat_sheet.heading: COLD OPEN · EXT. ABANDONED DESERT MOTEL – LAST LIGHT (0:56-1:12, V01)
beat_sheet.what_happens: But she can't bring him in until she knows the place is still hers. VENUS wants proof that nobody has found the motel since she left it. She stops in the carport, leans across JEAN's knees, takes the pistol from the glovebox where she left it outside the bar (SC04) and slides it into her back pocket. She walks the frontage alone, tugs the padlock on the office door and checks the dust on its step, which is unbroken. Only then does she unload his black bag, her bag and the grocery sacks and shoulder open the swollen door of a ground-floor room. JEAN stays in the passenger seat with his head to the door. Detail: the untouched dust on the office step is her proof.
beat_sheet.turn: From arming herself and checking to unloading: the place is still hers.

beat_sheet.heading: COLD OPEN · INT. MOTEL ROOM – NIGHT (1:12-1:30, V01; LIMERENCE TITLE ON FINAL FRAME)
beat_sheet.what_happens: So she sets up house. VENUS wants the table set for two. By one battery lantern her hands set out cans, water jugs, oranges and a palm-sized photo printer, then pull a second chair up to the table. A bedroll on the floor and a row of emptied jugs by the door show she has been living here. Above the table is a wall of long-lens photos of JEAN: at a bar window, at a gas pump, crossing a street. He is alone in every one, and none show the two of them together. The frame holds on the table, the two chairs and the wall until nothing moves. LIMERENCE title. Detail: the photo printer, planted for SC18.
beat_sheet.turn: From breaking into a derelict motel to setting a table for two in a room she has lived in for weeks.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. VENUS'S CAR (THE SAME OPEN TWO-SEATER, TOP UP), ACROSS FROM A DIVE BAR – THURSDAY NIGHT, THE NIGHT BEFORE (1:30-3:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: The wall was shot from far off, and this is how. VENUS wants to go in before JEAN, drunk over his breakup for the third night running, leaves alone again. Parked across the street, she films him through the bar window, alone at the counter. On her passenger seat are a rubber-banded stack of long-lens prints of him going back months and a photocopied incident report with a woman's name blacked out and 'NO FURTHER ACTION' stamped across it (fictional). Tactic 1: she zooms in on his face as far as the lens goes. Tactic 2: she waits, and he signals for another. But the BARTENDER, who wants to close Jean's tab, sets the tab slip in front of him. She takes the pistol from her back pocket and shuts it in the glovebox beside a small closed metal tin, then takes the tin and pockets it. The pistol stays in the glovebox until the motel (SC02). Detail: she trades the gun for the tin.
beat_sheet.turn: From watching him through a lens to walking into his frame without the gun.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. DIVE BAR – CONTINUOUS (3:00-5:30) · INCITING INCIDENT
beat_sheet.what_happens: So she sits down beside him. VENUS wants JEAN to agree to play her game. JEAN wants to finish his drink without being seen. She opens with a test she already knows the answer to. VENUS: 'Have we met before?' JEAN: 'No. Not that I'm aware of.' VENUS: 'Hmm. You seem down. Why don't we play a game?' JEAN: 'Sure.' She lays one straw flat in the wet ring his glass left on the counter. VENUS: 'It's called decorum. The goal is to figure out if the house we build would last. We ask each other questions. Agree, we get a stick. Don't, we take a drink and lose one.' The house is straws laid flat on the counter: four walls and a pitched roof. He stalls with a counter. JEAN: 'Sure we can play, but you haven't gotten your drink yet.' BARTENDER, who wants the order taken and the tab closed: 'What can I get you guys?' VENUS: 'How about I get this first round. Two Naked and Famous.' JEAN: 'So what is in a Naked and Famous?' VENUS: 'Something that'll make you famous for being naked.' Her hand lands on his forearm. VENUS: 'Kidding. Mezcal with a touch of personality. Too strong? I can have him change it to a mimosa.' He props himself up. JEAN: 'Ah. Someone with a little character.' He slides the tab slip back to the BARTENDER unsigned. JEAN: 'Let the game begin. Cheers to having some decorum.' VENUS: 'Cheers.' Detail: the first straw lies in the wet ring from his glass.
beat_sheet.turn: From a man drinking to be left alone to a man pushing back his tab and raising a glass to her game.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. DIVE BAR – LATER (5:30-8:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: But the game she runs is a trial he doesn't know he's in. JEAN wants to be the wronged man in her eyes. VENUS wants to hear him tell the truth about his ex. JEAN: 'First question. What is your name, and what do you think it means?' VENUS: 'I was wondering when you'd ask. Venus. Apparently some Roman goddess of love. What about you?' JEAN: 'St. Jean. But just call me J, it's easier.' VENUS: 'I've met a saint. The Lord has answered my prayers. I think we just earned a stick toward our home.' She lays a second straw flat against the first: a wall. VENUS: 'Why do you look so defeated?' JEAN: 'Damn, I'm that easily read. You see it in my eye or my face?' VENUS: 'I felt it in your soul. Damaged, like you'd just been slayed.' She laughs. VENUS: 'A true martyr on a Thursday night, alone in an empty bar. Who slayed you, my friend?' JEAN: 'She left. Packed while I was at work. I never once raised my voice.' VENUS drinks and pulls the wall straw back out. JEAN: 'That's a no?' VENUS: 'That's a drink.' She closes the gap between the stools and leans to his ear. VENUS: 'Why do they call you a saint? Are you willing to save me?' She pulls back, laughing. VENUS: 'I'm just fucking with you. My turn.' His flaw under pressure: he lies to stay the victim. Detail: he denies something nobody asked him.
beat_sheet.turn: From a straw earned to a straw taken: her first verdict, which he hears as flirting.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT. DIVE BAR – LATER, BY THE CANDLE (8:00-9:45)
beat_sheet.what_happens: But she wants a reason to let him pass. JEAN wants to take her home tonight, and he takes her turn: he pulls the bar candle between them so he can see her eyes. JEAN: 'Let's go deeper.' VENUS: 'Sure. My heart's an open book, if you want to read it.' JEAN: 'What makes you tingle inside?' VENUS: 'Ahh. Good one.' She holds his eyes. VENUS: 'A man who doesn't have any fear and is willing to tame a beast.' JEAN: 'What dog doesn't want a true owner?' He picks up a straw and, instead of laying it flat, stands it upright in the candle's soft wax: a chimney he awards himself. Her fingertip rests on top of it, then slides away, and it stays standing. VENUS: 'Who would have known a stranger could be my next lover?' A three-second cut at real speed: her hand on a black shirt against white sheets, no nudity. She shakes her head and is back at the bar. Detail: the chimney straw standing in candle wax.
beat_sheet.turn: From judge to lover: her fingertip leaves standing a straw she should have pulled.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT ONE · INT./EXT. DIVE BAR, THROUGH THE WINDOW, THEN THE STREET – LAST CALL (9:45-11:00) · ACT ONE OUT
beat_sheet.what_happens: So the house never settles. Seen silent through the window and cut on the laughs, the flat outline grows when he adds a straw and shrinks when she pulls one. Once it has its whole roof; on the next drink her fingertip draws a roof straw out of the line (the S03 frame), and he laughs. Inside at last call, the counter is bare except for the chimney, upright in the candle wax: the only straw still standing. JEAN wants a picture of the night. He holds his phone out at arm's length to get the two of them and the chimney in one frame. VENUS takes the phone from his hand, photographs him alone beside the upright straw and hands it back without a word. The BARTENDER wants the counter cleared and reaches for the glasses. JEAN wants to end the game as the winner and reaches for the chimney. VENUS plucks it first and slides it into her jacket pocket beside the tin. They walk out with their arms tangled and climb into an unbranded rideshare, leaving her two-seater parked across the street. Detail: the last straw standing in candle wax.
beat_sheet.turn: From his phone framing the two of them to a photo of him alone and the last straw in her pocket: she has him, and the verdict is still open.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. RIDESHARE BACK SEAT – NIGHT, DASH CAM (11:00-12:30)
beat_sheet.what_happens: But the tin and the straw are in the pocket his hands go for. Seen from the dash cam, its timestamp running in the corner, they kiss and grab at each other in the back seat with their clothes on. The DRIVER wants his back seat kept clean: he flicks the dome light on, then watches in the mirror. VENUS reaches up and flicks it off. JEAN wants his hands inside her jacket, and his hand finds the pocket with the tin in it. She takes his wrist and moves his hand to her waist, laughing against his mouth. Detail: the dash cam is a second recording of him, one she doesn't control.
beat_sheet.turn: From his hand on the tin to her hand steering it away: the tin stays hers to open.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. VENUS'S BUILDING, LOBBY AND STAIRS TO HER DOOR – NIGHT (12:30-14:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: So he arrives with questions. JEAN wants to know who she is and how she pays for this, but he wants the night more. He takes in the marble lobby and the quiet stairwell. JEAN: 'So what do you-' VENUS: 'Mind the step.' He lets it go. VENUS wants him inside without questions and leads up the stairs a step ahead. VENUS: 'Please don't judge me. It's a little messy.' JEAN: 'We aren't all perfect. Who said Rome was built in a day?' She opens the door on an all-white apartment: white floor, white furniture, no dust anywhere. He stands on the threshold in all black. JEAN: 'I happened to miss the mess. Can I use your bathroom?' VENUS: 'Of course. Right on the left. I'm gonna change and make us something to drink.' Detail: she lines his black shoes up on the white mat by the door.
beat_sheet.turn: From a man with questions to a man who stops asking and walks in.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, BATHROOM – NIGHT (14:00-15:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: But the white room has a flaw. JEAN wants to get back out to her fast. He grins at himself in the mirror and checks his teeth. He lifts the white toilet seat: a few small dried red drops on the back of the rim, left from the previous man (A13) and never explained on screen. He tears off toilet paper and wipes, looks at the faint pink on the tissue, drops it in the bowl and flushes. Through the door, ice drops into glasses. Detail: he checks his teeth before he deals with the blood.
beat_sheet.turn: From a man who finds blood to a man who wipes it away and walks out smiling.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, LIVING ROOM – NIGHT (15:00-17:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: So she sets her last question. JEAN wants her in the bedroom now. VENUS wants to ask the last question first. She waits in an oversized team T-shirt with no logo, bare legs, a drink in each hand; the chimney straw from the bar stands upright in the ice of her own glass. JEAN: 'Did you miss me?' VENUS: 'You haven't shown me anything worth missing.' He takes the other glass, downs it like a shot and blows out hard. JEAN: 'Whew!' VENUS: 'You alright, champ?' JEAN: 'I ain't won a ring yet.' She sets her glass on the white table, the straw still standing, and slides a small metal tin across to him, closed. He turns it over like a prize and tries the lid, but her fingertip stays on it. VENUS: 'Let's take a trip.' JEAN: 'Like the one where we get on a plane, or the one where we have a good time?' VENUS: 'Both. You feel like this space isn't safe?' JEAN: 'No. Not at all.' Detail: the bar straw standing in her ice.
beat_sheet.turn: From a drink he can swallow to a tin he can't open: the last straw stands again, in her glass.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT TWO · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, LIVING ROOM – CONTINUOUS (17:00-20:00) · ACT TWO OUT
beat_sheet.what_happens: But he answers with a line. VENUS wants one true thing about love: his last straw. JEAN wants to get her to the bedroom. VENUS: 'Trust is a thing that is earned. You can't assume things are great. What's glamorous can be a trap for a black hole. Do you think love is built on trust or lust? What makes one lust, the words or the sex appeal?' He inches closer and puts his hand on her thigh. JEAN: 'Hmm.' VENUS: 'Who is to say love has a conditional standard? Who is to say lust doesn't have great intentions? Who created the standard of what's wrong or right?' He reaches for a comeback. JEAN: 'Why does love have to be right or wrong? Why does pain have to be felt? Words have made me stronger, yet pain has made me hopeless. Everyone's standard must belong to who they are within.' VENUS: 'How does that correlate to love, or what I just asked?' JEAN: 'That's for you to find out.' She draws the straw out of her ice and lays it flat on the white table, where it leaves a wet mark. She lifts her fingertip off the tin and opens the lid toward him. What's inside stays out of frame. Detail: the wet mark the straw leaves on the white table.
beat_sheet.turn: From a straw standing in her ice to a straw lying flat and the tin open: he gave her a line, and the house is down.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, HALL TO BEDROOM – NIGHT (20:00-21:30)
beat_sheet.what_happens: So the sentence begins, and the room gives him a second warning. JEAN wants to get her to the bed. He lifts VENUS and carries her toward the bedroom, past the open tin and the flat straw on the table. At the white threshold he looks down: three small dried red drops on the floor. He stops for half a step. VENUS wants him to keep walking; she never looks down. She turns his face back to hers. VENUS: 'J.' He steps over the drops and carries her through. Detail: the drops are at the threshold, where she never looks.
beat_sheet.turn: From stopping at the drops to stepping over them.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, BEDROOM AND BATHROOM – LATER THAT NIGHT (21:30-24:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: But his breathing won't let her rest. Afterwards, JEAN sleeps face-down in the white sheets, breathing slow and loud, his black clothes on the white floor. VENUS wants to stop hearing his breathing. Tactic 1: she folds his black clothes square on a white chair. Tactic 2: in the bathroom she opens the mirror cabinet. Inside is a four-week pill organiser with every lid still shut and full, and a pharmacy label turned to the wall. She opens one lid, looks, closes it and puts the organiser back. No drug name, no diagnosis. She lies down beside him. His breathing stops for a long gap, then catches with a rasp. Her phone lies on the nightstand beside a small white speaker. Tactic 3: her hand passes the phone, puts a trance-soul track on low from the speaker, then turns it up until his breathing is under the music. Detail: weeks of full compartments.
beat_sheet.turn: From a breath that catches while he could still be helped to the music turned up over it: she reaches past her phone and stays in bed.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. WHITE APARTMENT, BEDROOM – MORNING (24:00-25:30)
beat_sheet.what_happens: But he doesn't wake. The track is still looping. JEAN lies face-down, mouth open, one arm off the bed, where he has lain since the night. VENUS lies awake beside him, a hand pressed to her forehead. She wants him to turn over and reach for her. Tactic 1: she waits through another loop of the track. Tactic 2: she lifts his arm over her waist, and it slides off. Tactic 3: VENUS: 'J. Stay for breakfast.' He doesn't move. She switches the music off, and the room is silent. Detail: the same four bars coming round again.
beat_sheet.turn: From waiting in the bed for him to turn over to getting up to strip it.

beat_sheet.heading: ACT THREE · INT. WHITE APARTMENT – DAY (25:30-28:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: So she cleans. VENUS wants the apartment spotless before she takes him away. She dresses JEAN in his black clothes, seats him in the white armchair and puts his sunglasses on him, a plant for SC01. She strips the bed and remakes it in fresh white sheets, pulling the corners tight and smoothing until no crease is left. But at the bedroom threshold she finds the three dried drops JEAN stepped over; she had missed them. She kneels and scrubs until the white cloth is pink and the floor is white, then folds the pink cloth into a square before she bins it. She closes the tin and pockets it with the flat straw. The frame holds on the finished room, with JEAN in black in the white chair, longer than is comfortable. Detail: the pink cloth folded square.
beat_sheet.turn: From a room she thought was clean to a flaw she missed and scrubs out: spotless, with a dead man in black at its centre.

beat_sheet.heading: TAG · INT. MOTEL ROOM – NIGHT, CONTINUOUS FROM THE COLD OPEN (28:00-30:00)
beat_sheet.what_happens: Back at the motel, VENUS wants to get into one photograph with JEAN. JEAN is already in the second chair at the table under his wall, with the lantern and oranges in front of him. She unhooks his sunglasses from her own neckline and sets them down by the oranges. From her bag she takes two long-lens prints of a different man on courthouse steps (fictional) and pins them at the edge of the wall, next to the last photos of JEAN. She sits close, rests her head on his shoulder and raises her phone. Her thumb goes to the flip-camera icon and this time presses it. The screen shows both of them: her face lit by the lantern, smiling, beside his open eyes, which aim past the lens. She turns his chin toward it with two fingers, and his eyes still miss it. She takes the photo anyway. The palm-sized printer whirs out a print, and she pins it between JEAN's photos and the new man's: the only photo of them together. This is the situation the series repeats. Detail: the printer's whir in a silent room.
beat_sheet.turn: From never in his frame to in it, while the wall already moves on to the next man.

deliverable_scripts.idea_in_one_line: She laughs and films a sleeping man across the desert until his open eyes show he is dead, then sets a table for two under a wall of his photos, none of them together.

beats.picture: Inside her phone's upright frame, centred in black: JEAN in the passenger seat of an open two-seater, cheek on the headrest, head turned to the door, so only his black collar, jaw and one arm of his sunglasses show. Low gold sun; the edge of an empty town slides by behind him. The picture jolts when she laughs.
beats.sound: Wind clipping the phone mic. VENUS's laugh, loud and right on the mic. No score.

beats.picture: Phone frame. The car rolls to a full stop at a stop sign on an empty crossroads with no other car in any direction; the sign sits behind his head. VENUS's free hand enters the frame, brushes dust off his black shirt and straightens his collar. He doesn't stir. The frame lurches as she drives on. [Fallback: her hand only rests on his collar.]
beats.sound: The engine idling, the wind dropped to nothing, her fingers brushing fabric close to the mic, then the engine pulling away.

beats.picture: Three jump cuts inside the phone frame, the timer jumping at each: empty storefronts, then open desert, then scrub hills pass behind JEAN, the gold sun lower every time. His head, collar and sunglasses never move between cuts.
beats.sound: The wind roar cut hard three times, each cut landing on a different snatch of her laugh.

beats.picture: Phone frame, sun low behind the car. Her thumb slides across the glass to the flip-camera icon in the corner, rests on it, then slides away. The lens stays on JEAN's turned head, and the frame shakes as she laughs. [Fallback: the screen flips to the front camera for under a second, catching both of them, her face cut off by the top edge and his head slumped against the door, sunglasses crooked; then it flips back to him.]
beats.sound: Wind on the mic. Her laugh, shorter.

beats.picture: Blue dusk inside the phone frame. The phone's small video light switches on and hits JEAN's black collar, and the fine desert dust on the fabric glints. His head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: The wind easing on the mic; tyres on grit underneath.

beats.picture: She lowers the phone to her lap and the picture opens to full width: the open two-seater alone on the dusk road, VENUS laughing at the wheel with her eyes on JEAN, whose head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: The wind drops away. Tyres and engine are heard from outside the car, and her laugh is further off now.

beats.picture: Full width, the car still moving. VENUS lifts the sunglasses off JEAN's face and, with them still in her hand, turns his chin toward her with two fingers. His eyes are open, pale and dusted; the wind moves his hair, and they do not blink. [Fallback, A16: the same action with the car parked at the motel.]
beats.sound: Tyres and engine. No laugh.

beats.picture: In the first second she hooks one open arm of the sunglasses into her neckline. She raises the phone and the picture narrows back to the upright frame, JEAN's open eyes centred under the video light. The frame shakes as she laughs. Her thumb goes to the flip-camera icon, rests there, then slides back. [Fallback: the front camera for under a second, her face lit by the video light beside his open eyes, which look past the lens; then it flips back to him.]
beats.sound: The wind comes back on the mic. Her laugh, softer and close.

beats.picture: Full width, last light: the two-seater stands in the carport of an abandoned motel under a peeling MOTEL sign on steel legs. VENUS leans across JEAN's knees, opens the glovebox, takes out a pistol and slides it into her back pocket. [Fallback: the pistol already in her back pocket, no hand on it.]
beats.sound: The cooling engine pinging, the glovebox latch dropping open, wind in dry palms.

beats.picture: Full width: VENUS walks the gutted motel frontage alone, the pistol grip showing from her back pocket, tugs the padlock on the office door and looks down at the unbroken dust on its step.
beats.sound: Gravel under her boots, a loose panel on the sign ticking in the wind, the padlock knocking on its hasp.

beats.picture: At the car VENUS lifts out his black bag, her own bag and two paper grocery sacks while JEAN stays in the passenger seat, head to the door. She carries them to a ground-floor room and shoulders its swollen door open.
beats.sound: The boot lid, paper sacks rustling, the door scraping open over grit.

beats.picture: Inside the room, one battery lantern on a wooden table; a bedroll on the floor and a row of emptied water jugs by the door. Her hands set down cans, full water jugs, oranges and a palm-sized photo printer, then pull a second chair up to the table. On the wall above are dozens of long-lens photos of JEAN, alone in every one; none show the two of them together.
beats.sound: The lantern switch clicking, cans set down on wood, a chair leg dragging across the boards.

beats.picture: A held frame in which nothing moves: the lantern, the oranges, the cans, the printer, two empty chairs, the bedroll and the emptied jugs by the door, and above the table the wall of JEAN photos, none of which include her.
beats.sound: Only the wind outside, pushing at the door.

beats.picture: The same held frame of the lantern-lit table, the two empty chairs, the bedroll and the wall of JEAN photos, with the LIMERENCE title card landing over it.
beats.sound: Silence.

deliverable_scripts.idea_in_one_line: Her phone keeps recording a man who never wakes; his open eyes show why, and her thumb won't turn the camera on herself.

beats.picture: The upright phone frame fills the screen: stopped at the stop sign, VENUS's hand brushes dust off JEAN's black shirt and straightens his collar while his head stays turned to the door.
beats.sound: Wind on the mic, fabric under her fingers.

beats.picture: Hard cut to the same pose inside the phone frame: JEAN's collar, jaw and sunglasses haven't moved, the open desert is behind him and the gold sun is much lower.
beats.sound: A burst of wind and a snatch of her laugh.

beats.picture: Blue dusk, the full-width shot reframed upright: VENUS lifts the sunglasses off JEAN's face and turns his chin toward her with two fingers, the dusk road behind them.
beats.sound: Tyres on grit and the engine, heard from outside the car.

beats.picture: Phone frame under the small video light: JEAN's eyes, open, pale and dusted, fill the frame, and the wind moves his hair while they do not blink.
beats.sound: Wind on the mic.

beats.picture: Her laugh shakes the phone frame side to side while JEAN's open eyes stay centred in it, unblinking, the timer still running.
beats.sound: Her laugh, soft and close to the mic.

beats.picture: Her thumb slides onto the flip-camera icon in the corner of the frame, rests there over his open eyes, then slides back off. [Fallback: the under-a-second flip to both of them, then back to him.]
beats.sound: Wind, then the mic cuts out.

beats.picture: The recording stops: the upright frame goes black, the red REC dot is gone, and the LIMERENCE title card sits centred in the dark.
beats.sound: Silence.

stills_copy.picture: Key art, 2:3. From behind VENUS's right shoulder at the wheel of the open two-seater in low gold sun: she laughs in three-quarter profile, and her raised phone shows JEAN under a red REC dot. Beside it the real JEAN sits pale and still in his black shirt, sunglasses on, head turned to the door. Two of him, none of her.
stills_copy.headline: LIMERENCE

stills_copy.picture: World frame, 16:9. The motel room by one battery lantern: a wall of dozens of long-lens photos of JEAN, alone in every one and none of them together. Below it, a table set with cans, water jugs, oranges and a palm-sized photo printer, two chairs pulled up; a bedroll on the floor and a row of emptied water jugs by the door.

Social frame, 4:5. A dim bar counter by candlelight: between two cocktail glasses, drinking straws lie flat on the wood in the outline of a house, four walls and a pitched roof, one wall straw in a wet ring, and VENUS's fingertip draws one roof straw out of the line.

decisions.choice: The pilot runs as a cold open, three acts and a tag across 18 scenes, about 30 minutes. The inciting incident ('Have we met before?') lands at about 3:00. Act One ends with the last straw going into her pocket, Act Two with the tin opening, and the tag with the first photo of them together.
decisions.reason: The pilot shape needs 12 or more scenes, the inciting incident in the first sixth and a last scene that shows what repeats. Venus's own choices resolve the climax twice: she opens the tin after his line (SC13), and she turns the music up over his catching breath (SC15).
decisions.source: Craft brief (pilot; the protagonist's choice resolves the climax); A01; A05; A06; A18; story seed

decisions.choice: The pilot runs on one continuous timeline. The bar (SC04) is Thursday night, the night before the drive. SC05-SC17 run on to the next day, the cold open is that evening, and the tag follows straight on from it. Her car in SC04 is the same open two-seater, with its top up. She shuts the pistol in its glovebox outside the bar and takes it out again at the motel (SC02, V01 56-60 s).
decisions.reason: The prints going back months already show how long she has watched him. The gun is accounted for all the way from the bar to her back pocket.
decisions.source: Reviewer note (continuity chain); verified fact (gun in her back pocket at the motel); premise

decisions.choice: V01 is SC01-SC03 and follows the order of the R2 execution example. Changes: the route's 56-64 s beat is split into the glovebox pistol (56-60 s) and the frontage check (60-64 s). B07 holds only the sunglasses lifted, the chin turned and the eyes. She hooks one open arm of the sunglasses into her neckline in the first second of B08, with no fold, and B08's frame shakes as she laughs. The table gets a photo printer and a second chair, and a bedroll and a row of emptied jugs by the door appear in B12, B13 and S02.
decisions.reason: The make-or-break eyes shot (A16) carries no extra hand action. V02-B05's shaking frame now exists in V01's footage. The cold open shows the room she has kept. The printer and chair come back in SC18.
decisions.source: Route R2 execution example and revision log; A14; A16; reviewer note on V01; brief V02 ('rebuilt from V01 footage')

decisions.choice: The sunglasses carry continuity: she puts them on him in SC17, lifts them off in V01-B07, hooks them into her neckline in B08, and sets them down by the oranges in SC18 before she sits.
decisions.reason: She can't lift off sunglasses she is already wearing. The object moves from him to her, so the tag opens with his face bare for the photo.
decisions.source: Reviewer note (continuity chain); craft brief (plant an object that comes back)

decisions.choice: V01 and V02 have no spoken lines, so every vo field is empty. Her laugh, written in the sound field, is the only voice.
decisions.reason: V01 is specified with 0 spoken or lip-synced lines, and V02 must read with the sound off.
decisions.source: A15; brief V01 and V02 labels

decisions.choice: The phone's REC timer goes in on_screen_text as on-screen UI added in finishing. LIMERENCE is the only title, on V01's final frame (88-90 s) and in V02's last 2 s.
decisions.reason: The timer carries the hour-long drive without words, and in V02 it carries the time passing. Generated footage can't be trusted to render legible digits.
decisions.source: Route R2 visual language; brief deliverables; craft brief (words the viewer must read go in on_screen_text)

decisions.choice: The straw house is defined once in SC05: straws laid flat on the counter as four walls and a pitched roof, the first straw in the wet ring from his glass. It gets its whole roof once and loses a roof straw (SC08, the same moment as S03). Jean's own straw stands upright in the candle wax as a chimney (SC07) and is the last one standing. In SC12 it stands again, in the ice of her glass. In SC13 she draws it out and lays it flat, leaving a wet mark on the white table, then lifts her fingertip off the tin.
decisions.reason: Production design can build it without asking, and D01 and S03 show the same house. The last straw goes from standing to lying flat, so the verdict reads with the sound off, and the tin opens only after it (A18).
decisions.source: Reviewer notes (house form; last straw); Lucas's straw game; A04; A18; brief S03

decisions.choice: R2's hesitation is carried into the bar while Jean is alive. In SC07 her fingertip rests on the chimney he awarded himself, then slides away, the same rest-and-slide as her thumb on the flip icon. In SC08 she takes his phone when he tries to frame them together, photographs him alone and hands it back without a word.
decisions.reason: The want to be in one photograph with him is tested before he dies, which plants SC18's front camera. The scene also reads as a killer's caution and seeds A17: the man she would turn the camera on while he is alive.
decisions.source: Route R2 central idea; reviewer note (R2 in the flashback); A17

decisions.choice: Jean's lie at decorum is a new line that Lucas did not write: 'She left. Packed while I was at work. I never once raised my voice.' It is followed by 'That's a no?' / 'That's a drink.'
decisions.reason: It shows decorum as a verdict without voiceover. He denies something nobody asked, she takes a straw, and he hears it as flirting.
decisions.source: A02; A04; craft brief (exposition as a weapon); taste note (restraint over explanation)

decisions.choice: In SC04 she trades the pistol for the tin. The dried blood on the toilet rim and the drops at the threshold belong to the previous man and are never explained on screen.
decisions.reason: This makes the tin her chosen method and leaves room for A13 without showing or telling it.
decisions.source: A05; A13; must avoid (showing how the tin's contents are prepared or dosed)

decisions.choice: SC15: Venus's want is to stop hearing his breathing. The organiser beat plays as written: every lid full, the label to the wall, no drug name or diagnosis. His breath then stops for a long gap and catches, and her hand passes her phone on the nightstand to turn the speaker up until his breathing is under the music.
decisions.reason: The want is now a verb and an object. The breath catch is something a microphone can record, so turning the music up reads as her choice to stay in bed while he could still be helped. The meds are seen but never given as the reason.
decisions.source: Reviewer note (SC15); craft brief (want as verb and object; the protagonist's choice resolves the climax); verified facts (meds untaken for weeks; trance-soul to quiet her); must avoid (meds as the explanation)

decisions.choice: The trance-soul track plays only from her speaker, in SC15-SC16, and she switches it off in SC16. Every other scene carries its own sound: wind, tyres, straws on wood, ice, a glovebox latch, a printer.
decisions.reason: The music stays inside the scene, and sound design leads everywhere else.
decisions.source: A08; tone (music); taste note (sound design before music)

decisions.choice: The horror in the white apartment is its tidiness: dried drops only, on the toilet rim and at the threshold. Jean wipes one set and Venus scrubs the other. What's in the tin stays out of frame. The frame holds on the finished room longer than is comfortable.
decisions.reason: The tone calls for clean horror with no spray, no gore and the method off screen, as in ref 05's calm next to horror (going by the brief's description).
decisions.source: Tone (clean); must avoid (gore; the tin's contents or dosing)

decisions.choice: Brands: the rideshare is unbranded, the T-shirt is an oversized team shirt with no logo, and Lucas's 'Cracker Jack' reference is dropped from Jean's reaction to the tin. 'Naked and Famous' stays as a cocktail name from Lucas's dialogue.
decisions.reason: Nothing is cleared yet. The producer confirms whether the cocktail name needs clearance.

decisions.choice: The only sex on screen is a three-second real-speed insert of her hand on a black shirt against white sheets, at the bar (SC07). The bedroom scenes start afterwards. There is none in V01, V02 or the stills.
decisions.reason: The pitch pieces must be able to circulate. There is no slow motion anywhere.
decisions.source: Must avoid (explicit sex; slow motion); Lucas's 'visions' and 'aftermath' beats

decisions.choice: The next man's photos are two long-lens prints of a fictional man on courthouse steps. She takes them from her bag in SC18 and pins them up before the printer runs. The photo of her and Jean then goes up between his wall and the new man's.
decisions.reason: The new photos come from somewhere on screen. They show the system lost him without any text, and they set up the situation the series repeats.
decisions.source: A06; reviewer note (continuity chain); craft brief (the last scene shows what repeats); must avoid (real cases)

decisions.choice: Taste notes followed: hands before faces (her face first at 34 s, Jean's only at 42 s as the one face shot); restraint over explanation (no voiceover or code; the meds, the blood and the phone passed on the nightstand are shown, never explained); sound design before music (no score in V01 or V02); dry over sentimental ('That's a drink'); one detail per scene, named in each. Broken on purpose: S01 shows her laughing face, because a poster needs its lead and the laugh beside a dead man is the performance that earns it. The fallbacks for V01-B04 and B08 also show part of her face for under a second, as the route already accepts.
decisions.reason: The notes ask for a flag wherever one is broken. 'The product is a tool, then a hero' doesn't apply because there is no product.

decisions.choice: S01 carries LIMERENCE only. S02 and S03 carry no text, so their headline and subline are left empty.
decisions.reason: The brief specifies 'LIMERENCE title only' for S01 and 'no text' for S02 and S03.

assumptions: The scene timings in the D01 headings are estimates for a roughly 30-minute half hour (A01). The director can adjust act lengths.

The car is left parked across from the bar when they take the rideshare (SC08). Fetching it and moving Jean from the apartment into the passenger seat happen off screen, between SC17 and SC01. If Lucas wants that shown, it becomes a short scene after SC17.

Creative additions in D01 for Lucas to approve or strike: the pistol traded for the tin, and the fictional incident report stamped 'NO FURTHER ACTION' (SC04); Venus speaking the decorum rules close to Lucas's own words, and the flat house of four walls and a pitched roof (SC05); the tab slip Jean pushes back (SC05); Jean's lie and 'That's a no?' / 'That's a drink.' (SC06); the chimney straw in the candle wax and her fingertip resting on it (SC07); his selfie attempt and the photo she takes of him alone (SC08); the dash-cam timestamp and dome light (SC09); 'Mind the step' and his shoes on the white mat (SC10); the straw standing in her ice (SC12) and its wet mark on the white table (SC13); the four-week organiser with its label turned to the wall, the breath catch and her hand passing the phone (SC15); 'J. Stay for breakfast.' (SC16); the sunglasses she puts on him and the drops she scrubs (SC17); the printer, the second chair and the courthouse-steps photos (SC03, SC18).

Additions in V01 beyond the route's execution example: the pistol taken from the glovebox (56-60 s, split from the route's 56-64 s beat); one open arm of the sunglasses hooked into her neckline (50-51 s); the photo printer, the second chair, the bedroll and the emptied jugs (72-90 s). Shouldering open a swollen door stands in for Lucas's 'breaks into the motel'.

In SC18 the next man's photos go up before the photograph of her and Jean, as the notes ask. She takes the photo even though Jean's eyes miss the lens, and the imperfect first photo is kept on purpose.
Lucas's dialogue is kept with light spelling and grammar cleanup ('The Lord has answered my prayers'). The trust/lust exchange is trimmed, not rewritten.
'Naked and Famous' is treated as a cocktail name, not a brand. The producer confirms this under A10.
The phone UI (REC dot, timer, flip-camera icon) is an original design added in finishing. Clearance is pending with the producer (A10) and is not claimed as cleared.
V02's timer readings after 01:04:55 (01:04:58, 01:05:00) assume the V01 50-56 s shot runs as one continuous take.

Jean, Venus, Jean's ex, the next man and every case are fictional. No character is modelled on a face in Lucas's references. No reference image was inspected in this run; they are cited only as the brief describes them.
The phrase Lucas used as an internal comparison does not appear in any deliverable.

blockers.issue: A16: Jean's open, unblinking eyes in a moving convertible (V01 42-56 s; V02 4-13 s) have not been tested for consistency. The glovebox reach across his knees (V01-B09) is a second hand-risk shot.
blockers.resolution: Run the 5 s test shot. If it fails, use the written fallback: the reveal (V01-B07) plays with the car parked at the motel. If the glovebox reach fails, use the B09 fallback, with the pistol already in her pocket. No story beat changes.

blockers.issue: Clearance for the phone UI and the brands is pending (A10).
blockers.resolution: If the UI reads as a real operating system, keep only the REC dot and timer, and play the hesitation as the under-a-second front-camera flip (fallbacks are written into V01-B04, V01-B08 and V02-B06). Confirm that 'Naked and Famous' needs no clearance.

blockers.issue: The creative additions listed in assumptions need Lucas's approval.
blockers.resolution: Approve or strike each item. Any of them can be removed without losing a turn, except two: the last-straw chain (SC07-SC08, SC12-SC13), which carries A18 and the season question, and the breath catch in SC15, which carries Venus's climactic choice.

evidence.specificity: Production design, sound and casting can break most of this down without a follow-up call. Example: "Inside is a four-week pill organiser with every lid still shut and full, and a pharmacy label turned to the wall. She opens one lid, looks, closes it and puts the organiser back. No drug name, no diagnosis." The straw house is now defined once and built the same way throughout: "The house is straws laid flat on the counter: four walls and a pitched roof." The V01 timer readings are consistent: REC 00:00:04, then 00:58:40, then 01:04:55, and V02's 01:04:58 and 01:05:00 fit its 3 s and 2 s beats. A director would still ask three questions, and they hold the score at 8, not 9. How does Jean get into the chair in SC18 ("JEAN is already in the second chair")? Where do "his sunglasses" (SC17) and "his black bag" (V01-B11) come from, since neither appears from SC04 to SC16? Where is the speaker before the climax needs it in SC15?
evidence.distinctiveness: Nothing here could be moved into another vigilante pilot unchanged. The straw chain is one object that keeps changing meaning. It starts in a wet ring. Then "He picks up a straw and, instead of laying it flat, stands it upright in the candle's soft wax: a chimney he awards himself. Her fingertip rests on top of it, then slides away." It goes into her pocket, then stands in her ice, and finally "She draws the straw out of her ice and lays it flat on the white table, where it leaves a wet mark." Route R2's flip-camera hesitation is now tested while Jean is alive: "VENUS takes the phone from his hand, photographs him alone beside the upright straw and hands it back without a word." The ending refuses the neat version: "She turns his chin toward it with two fingers, and his eyes still miss it. She takes the photo anyway." Smaller details are just as specific to this story: the stop sign nobody else will reach, "That's a drink.", and the pink cloth folded square before she bins it.
evidence.fit: Lucas's idea is recognizable throughout and sharper than he wrote it. His bar dialogue survives almost word for word ("Who slayed you, my friend?"). Every must-include is present. The flip-camera icon at the ending pays off route R2 and A06: "Her thumb goes to the flip-camera icon and this time presses it." The must-avoids hold: no voiceover, no slow motion, the tin's contents "stay out of frame", the brands are unbranded and flagged under A10, and the meds are "seen, never named". Two gaps keep this at 8. First, the brief's D01 label includes "Season question (A17): the one man who tells the truth at decorum and seems to love her back, and whether she can sentence him", but the outline never states it; it only shows up in the decisions as "seeds A17". Second, the premise and story seed give Venus the beat "At the motel she seats Jean at the table", and SC18 skips it: "JEAN is already in the second chair."
evidence.craft: All six previous notes were addressed. (1) The continuity chain now holds. SC04 reads "THURSDAY NIGHT, THE NIGHT BEFORE". The car is "THE SAME OPEN TWO-SEATER, TOP UP". The pistol goes into the glovebox in SC04 and comes out in SC02/V01-B09. In SC18 she "unhooks his sunglasses from her own neckline", and the courthouse prints come "from her bag". (2) The last straw goes from standing in her ice to lying flat with a wet mark before the tin opens. (3) The house is defined once in SC05, and S03 is redrawn to match it. (4) The rest-and-slide at the bar and the refused selfie are in. (5) V01-B07 now carries only the eyes. The hook moves to "In the first second" of B08, B08 adds "The frame shakes as she laughs", and the bedroll and jugs appear in B12, B13 and S02. (6) SC15's want is now "to stop hearing his breathing", with a breath catch the microphone can record: "His breathing stops for a long gap, then catches with a rasp." The climax turns on her choice, and every scene is written as a readable "From X to Y". What remains is small but real. SC18 is "CONTINUOUS FROM THE COLD OPEN", yet V01 ends on "two empty chairs" with Jean still in the car. The speaker that decides the climax first appears in SC15. Jean's sunglasses and bag are never planted. A few actions don't hold up physically; note 5 lists them. A senior screenwriter would send this today with these notes.

notes.target: D01 SC11-SC12 and SC15 (the trance-soul track and the speaker)
notes.note: Venus's deciding tool first appears at the climax, so nothing plants it. Lucas's premise also has the track quiet her before the tin ('a trance-soul track quiets her. She slides over her metal tin'). SC11: under the ice dropping into glasses, add the same track starting low from the small white speaker; Venus puts it on while Jean is in the bathroom. SC12: it is still playing low when he comes out. Let it end, or have her stop it, before SC14. SC15: she turns the same track back on and turns it up until his breathing is under it. The object then returns with a new meaning: what quieted her now covers him. Update the decision that says the track 'plays only from her speaker, in SC15-SC16'. This stays inside the scene (A08).
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Plant what the climax needs before the midpoint, at least a scene ahead. The best plant is an object that comes back meaning something else'; premise; verified fact 'Trance-soul music plays to quiet her from feeling crazy'; A08

notes.target: D01 SC18 (series engine and season question)
notes.note: The brief's D01 label includes the season question, but the outline never states it. After 'This is the situation the series repeats', add two plain outline sentences. Engine: each episode opens on her phone recording the next man, and the front camera turns on once per man, at this table, afterwards. Season question (A17): the one man who tells the truth at decorum and seems to love her back, and whether she can sentence him. Frame the R2 version, 'the man she turns the front camera on while he is still alive', as a proposal for Lucas, since the route marked it 'not yet in D01'. Name SC08's refused selfie as its plant.
notes.source: Brief D01 label ('Season question (A17)'); route R2 recurring device and season-extension note; craft brief pilot ('the last scene shows the situation the series will repeat')

notes.target: D01 SC18 opening (seating Jean)
notes.note: The heading says 'CONTINUOUS FROM THE COLD OPEN', but V01-B11 leaves Jean in the passenger seat and B13-B14 hold on 'two empty chairs'. SC18 then opens with him 'already in the second chair'. The premise gives Venus this beat ('At the motel she seats Jean at the table'), and it pays off the chair she pulled up in V01-B12. Open SC18 on it as one readable action, then the sunglasses. For example: she backs him out of the car under the arms and drags him inside, his heels drawing two lines through the grit at the door, and lowers him into the second chair. Keep it to roughly the first 20 s of the scene's two minutes.
notes.source: Premise and story seed ending; quality bar craft ('continuity that holds'); craft brief ('the best plant is an object that comes back')

notes.target: D01 SC05 and SC17, V01-B11, S03 (Jean's sunglasses and bag, the house in S03)
notes.note: Nothing from SC04 to SC16 gives Jean sunglasses or a bag, yet SC17 puts 'his sunglasses on him' and V01-B11 unloads 'his black bag'. Plant both. In SC05, add his sunglasses hooked in the open collar of his black shirt at night; then B08, where she hooks them into her own neckline, puts them where he wore them. In SC17, she packs his phone, wallet and keys into a black bag by the door; alternatively, change B11 to 'two of her bags'. S03 is the SC08 moment, when the chimney already stands in the candle's wax, so add it at the edge of the S03 frame. Otherwise D01 and S03 again show different houses.
notes.source: Quality bar craft (continuity); craft brief ('plant what the climax needs'); previous review note ('D01 and S03 have to show the same house')

notes.target: V01-B09, D01 SC07, V01-B07 / SC17 / SC18 (physical plausibility)
notes.note: (a) In B09 she is seated at the wheel and can't slide a pistol into her back pocket. Write that she takes it from the glovebox, steps out and pockets it as she stands; the fallback is unchanged. (b) In SC07, a straw standing in the melt pool of a lit candle through a whole night at the bar would soften or catch fire. Stand it in the wax that has run down and set on the candle's saucer, and keep 'upright in the candle wax' in SC08. (c) He dies overnight in SC15. Dressing him in SC17, then turning his chin with two fingers at dusk (V01-B07, about 16 hours later) and again in SC18, runs against rigor, which the true-crime-following viewer will know about. Don't change the route's shot. Log it in the assumptions as a deliberate licence for Lucas and the director, next to the A16 test.
notes.source: Quality bar craft ('nothing physically implausible'); brief audience ('someone who follows true-crime cases online')

characters.role_in_story: Principal. A vigilante who watches unpunished men for months, then plays decorum with them over a date. She films everything and is never in her own frame. V01 objective: get JEAN to look back at her through her phone. Pilot want: one true thing about love from him, then one photograph with him. Obstacle: he is the man she is sentencing, he answers with lines, and by the cold open he is dead. Change: from never being in his frame to the first photo of them together (SC18), while the wall moves on to the next man. Age 30-38, target 34. Every face reads 30+ at the bar (alcohol, no market code given), and she is old enough to have kept a wall for months and paid for the white apartment. Defaults: I keep Lucas's height, slimness and long brown hair with highlights. I break the genre default (a glossy femme fatale in her late 20s) and the generator's stock face (symmetrical, poreless, smiling at the lens) with pores, laugh lines, one higher brow and marked working hands. She smiles at him, never at us. Heritage: Black American, recorded and never prompted. It is a choice, not a story need; Lucas to confirm (see blockers). Restate it if the setting is Toronto.
characters.screen_presence: In one frame: a woman in her mid-thirties drives with one hand and holds a phone up at arm's length toward the man beside her. Her shoulders are loose and her eyes are on him, not the road. The read: in love, not driving. Her hands lead (taste note: hands before faces). They brush dust off his collar and straighten it, and a thumb rests on the flip icon before it slides away. She handles things slowly, and what she puts on a surface lands square: cans on the table, his shoes on the mat, the pink cloth folded before she bins it. Between actions she is still and watching. She laughs with her whole torso, so the phone shakes. At the bar she sits turned fully to him, elbows off the counter, one fingertip on the straws. She never looks down at the drops.
characters.performance_style: Naturalistic, played as a love story. The laugh is the only heightened thing: real, from the belly, never a cackle. One laugh voice is locked across V01, V02 and D01: low, breaking high at the end, non-verbal. It syncs to her face only at 34-42 s and in the front-camera fallbacks, and it softens after the eyes (B08). At rest her face stays pleasant and busy with him. No knowing glance, no half-closed stare, no lip bite (taste note: restraint over explanation). Blink: at the bar she blinks less than he does. Beside the dead JEAN she blinks normally, so in a shared frame her blink is the one difference between them. Lens rule: her eyes never go into any lens. That includes the under-a-second flips in the B04 and B08 fallbacks, where they stay on him. The first time is SC18, when she looks into her own front camera while his eyes aim past it. D01: sync dialogue, dry and quick. She plays the bar flirt as genuine because she hopes he will pass (A18), and her verdicts land with no change of face ('That's a drink'). Registers without the laugh: SC15, the organiser gets the same face and hands as the padlock check (V01-B10). She opens one lid, looks and closes it, with no wince, no tremor and no pause on the turned label, so the meds are seen and never played as the reason. SC16 (ref 06, as the brief describes it) is the one scene where her hands have nothing to do. She lies still, a hand to her forehead, eyes on the back of his head, not the ceiling. She says 'J. Stay for breakfast.' at the same dry pitch as 'That's a drink', not pleading. SC17: she cleans with the same unhurried care she gave his collar. Repeated gesture: a digit rests, then slides off. Her thumb does it on the flip icon; her fingertip does it on the chimney straw and on the tin. Its central use is SC12-SC13, where her fingertip holds the tin's lid shut, then lifts off after his line. SC18 is the first time she presses.

The V01 neckline holds one open arm of the sunglasses (B08, SC18). The bar jacket pocket takes a small tin and a straw with no visible bulge (SC08-SC09). characters.role_in_story: Principal. St. Jean, called J: a serial dater three nights into drinking over a breakup. His ex's domestic-violence report went nowhere (A02, fictional). Bar objective: win the game and take her home. Apartment objective: get her to the bedroom. Want: to stay the wronged man in her eyes and win the night. Obstacle: every lie costs him a straw, and she already knows the answers. Change: from alive to dead, and from trying to frame the two of them (SC08) to being framed with her once he can no longer look (SC18). His V01 job is to be carried: dead weight, with the one face shot at 42 s. Age 34-42, target 38. Lines and a thickening waist show the charm is older than the looks it was built on. This breaks the category default (a sculpted late-20s leading man) and the generator's drift toward young and symmetrical, so his 'hit list' swagger reads as habit. Heritage: Haitian-American, recorded and never prompted. The reason is the name St. Jean and the family D01 can give him. Because heritage is not prompted, it cannot show in his face. He is Black like VENUS so the killing doesn't read as a cross-racial story the pilot isn't telling. Lucas to confirm with S01 and V02 in view (see blockers).
characters.screen_presence: In one frame: a big man in black slumped against the passenger door, cheek on the headrest, turned away from her camera so only his left jaw, ear, neck and collar show. Nothing moves but his hair, and he could be asleep. Alive at the bar, he starts with shoulders rounded over the glass, elbow planted, tab slip within reach: a man drinking to be left alone. When she speaks he props up, turns his stool to her and pulls the candle over. His hands grab and claim: straws, one stood upright for himself, his phone held out to frame them both, her pocket. His eyes go to price and surfaces (the lobby marble, the white room) before they go to her. He checks his teeth before he deals with the blood.
characters.performance_style: Two registers. Alive (SC04-SC15): naturalistic, a charmer running on habit. He laughs a beat before his own punchlines, and his eyes drift to her mouth and the room. At rest he is slack and heavy with drink until she gives him a game. Sync dialogue, delivered as if rehearsed. The SC06 lie ('I never once raised my voice') comes out easy, with no tell, because he believes it. The white-apartment speech is a man stretching for depth and missing. SC15 is breathing only, recorded wild: slow and loud, one long stop, then a rasp. He is face down, so there is no lip-sync. Dead (V01, SC16-SC18, S01): absolute stillness. No blink, no swallow, no breath in the chest. His eyes are open the same amount in every shot, upper lid at the top edge of the iris, aimed past the lens and never into it. Rigor, an assumption from the timeline (dead most of a day by dusk): his neck is set, so his head never bobs over the road or shifts between cuts. When she turns his chin, no muscle helps. The head gives a few degrees, the shoulders turn with it, and it stops there with no loll. That is why his eyes land past her (B07) and past her front camera (SC18). In SC16's morning his arm is still loose enough to slide off her waist. Silent in V01 and V02.
characters.wardrobe_fit_notes: 184 cm: 7 cm taller than VENUS, 14 cm taller than BARTENDER, 4 cm taller than DRIVER. Broad shoulders well wider than the hips, thick neck, waist thickening over the belt. He must plausibly lift and carry VENUS (177 cm, slim) in SC14. Right-handed: he holds the phone out and stands the straw with his right hand (SC07-SC08). US men's L, 36 waist (US sizing assumed). Constraints: one black outfit carries SC04-SC18, because she dresses him again in SC17. The black must read as one mass against white rooms and gold light, yet let dust glint at the collar (V01-B05). The collar stands clear of the jaw with his cheek on the headrest, so collar and jaw read as two shapes in 0-42 s. Nothing rides up or gapes while he slumps as dead weight through the cold open. His face must take sunglasses with one arm visible from his left side. His seated head must clear a small 1950s two-seater's windscreen (A11; production design confirms).
visual_identity_anchors: [macro] Build: 184 cm, broad shoulders well wider than the hips, thick neck, waist thickening over the belt.

[macro] Natural hair black #17110E, tight 4A curls, dense; squared hairline with the left temple receding further than the right. Worn 8-10 cm on top so the wind can lift it (V01-B07, V02-B04), tapered short at the sides; close beard with a hard cheek line to define the jaw in the turned-head frames (joint lock, stylist; top length subject to the A16 wind check).

[micro] Short, wide face, wide square jaw, heavy low brows that almost meet; irises dark brown #2A1A12, unchanged in death. Dead eyes (V01-B07, B08, V02-B04 to B06, SC18): the upper lid rests at the top edge of the iris in every shot; the cornea is dry and dulled with a faint grey film and no wet shine; dust sits on the lashes. 'Pale, lost' lives in these details, never in a lighter iris (joint lock, makeup/VFX).

[micro] Skin #6E4631 at the cheekbone, visible pores on the nose and cheeks, two faint forehead lines, crow's feet. Dead state (V01, SC16-SC18, S01): the same hex desaturated, grey-ash at the lips, lids and under the eyes, dust in the skin creases; never lightened (joint lock, stylist/makeup).

characters.role_in_story: Supporting, one line. Works the dive bar's Thursday late shift. Objective: close JEAN's tab and clear the counter before last call. What only he does: his tab slip is what sends VENUS in (SC04), and the order goes through him. Age 46-54, target 50: well past 30 for the alcohol rule, and twelve years older than JEAN. Both onlookers are men because the script calls each 'him' or 'he'. Heritage: Mexican-American, recorded and never prompted. It is a choice, not a story need: the two onlookers are cast apart from each other and from the leads, so no heritage is tied to one job.
characters.screen_presence: In one frame: a thick-set man of about fifty behind the bar, forearms on the counter, eyes on the tab. He wants to close up. He flicks the slip over face-down in front of JEAN without looking at it or at him, pours without watching, and reaches for glasses the moment they are empty. Nothing he puts down lands straight. He looks at the couple only when an order is due.
characters.performance_style: Understated, deadpan. At rest his eyes are on the tab, the glasses and the till. One sync line ('What can I get you guys?'), said half to the counter. No reaction to the flirt. At last call he clears glasses without a word; in the SC08 window shots he is background only.

characters.role_in_story: Featured, silent. A rideshare driver on a night shift, unbranded (A10). Objective: keep his back seat clean; the dome light is his only move. What only he does: he watches them without being part of her game, and his dash cam is the one recording of JEAN that she doesn't control. Age 58-64, target 61 (under 70, so no flag). His silver crown makes him the oldest face and reads at dash-cam resolution. Heritage: white American, recorded and never prompted. It is a choice, for the same reason as BARTENDER's.
characters.screen_presence: In one frame, from the cabin-facing dash cam on the windscreen: a thin, grey-haired man sitting upright at the edge of frame, both hands on the wheel, his outline against his side window as streetlight slides past. His right hand rises to the dome switch and flicks it on with one finger; he doesn't turn his head. When VENUS switches it off he leaves it off, and his eyes keep lifting to the mirror.
characters.performance_style: Understated, silent. He judges with his eyes only: they lift to the mirror, hold for about two seconds, then go back to the road. No reaction face and no words. The dash-cam frame is his whole performance space.

He is 4 cm shorter than JEAN and 3 cm taller than VENUS, but never stands beside either. Narrow, sloping shoulders; thin arms. Right-handed: his right hand goes to the dome switch. US men's M. Constraints: his head and shoulders must read as a clear silhouette against the driver's side window and passing streetlight at dash-cam resolution. His right sleeve stays clear of the wrist so the hand reads when it rises into the dome light. Nothing branded on him or the car (A10).

assumptions: The cast is exactly the script's four IDs: VENUS, JEAN, BARTENDER and DRIVER. The next man in the courthouse-steps prints (SC18) is not cast; he appears in photos only. Production design supplies two long-lens prints of a fictional man who must not share JEAN's build or hair or resemble any real person, and he gets a profile when episode 2 is written. JEAN's ex (name blacked out) is never on screen, and there is no VO character.

Setting: the script never names a country. The '-American' heritages, the US sizes and the assumed alcohol minimum of 25 all rest on a US setting, which the desert drive and motel fit. Lucas's Raptors shirt points to Toronto. If the city is Toronto, the heritages restate as Canadian (Black Canadian, Haitian-Canadian, Mexican-Canadian, white Canadian) with no change to any anchor, the sizes convert, and the 30+ reading floor stands. Lucas or the producer to confirm.
Alcohol rule: no market code was given, so the minimum is assumed to be 25 and every visible face reads 30+. Targets are 34, 38, 50 and 61, and bar background patrons in SC05-SC08 also read 30+.

Heritage: all four are casting choices, not script requirements. None goes into an anchor or a prompt, so none can show in a face. JEAN's reason is his name and the family D01 can give him. VENUS is matched to him so the killing doesn't read as a cross-racial story. BARTENDER and DRIVER are cast apart from each other and from the leads. Proposal for D01: the men she sentences vary in heritage across the season, so 'the man the system lost' is never tied to one heritage.

Lucas's 'tall slim model straight off your latest Vogue cover' is kept as height, slimness and bearing, not a glossy finish, because the tone rejects the glossy femme fatale. His optional blonde highlights are kept as a joint lock with the stylist.

'Pale' on JEAN comes from desaturation, grey-ash at the lips and lids, dust, a dry, grey-filmed cornea and unblinking eyes. It never comes from a lighter skin or iris hex, so the generator doesn't lighten a Black man's skin to signal death.

JEAN's identifying mole and hairline asymmetry are on his left side because his head is turned to the passenger door, away from VENUS. In 0-42 s the camera sees only his left jaw, ear, neck and collar.

Proposal for the director (blocking is the director's call): the phone in VENUS's left hand and her right hand for the touches (collar, sunglasses, chin), in a left-hand-drive car. The anchors are built for this: the left-thumb nick reads over the screen UI, and the right-hand scar reads in the touches. If the phone changes hands or the car is right-hand drive, mirror the pair. Both marks are permanent either way.

Rigor is a timeline assumption, not a medical claim. JEAN dies in the small hours and is filmed at dusk most of a day later, so his neck is played as set from V01 through SC18: no bob, and the head gives only a few degrees with the shoulders. This also explains why his head never moves between B03's cuts in a moving car. SC16's loose arm is read as early morning, before the limbs set. In SC17 she dresses him, seats him in the armchair and puts his sunglasses on, which runs against the stiffening. This is flagged to the director and writer: play it as effortful, or move the dressing earlier.
Squaring objects belongs to VENUS alone as the clean-horror tell. BARTENDER puts things down off-angle, and JEAN turns his stool rather than 'squaring' to her.

No reference was inspected; I worked only from the brief's descriptions. To stay clear of them, JEAN has no locs and no arm tattoo (ref 06), VENUS is not pale or auburn (ref 04), and no one is modelled on any face in refs 01-11.

VENUS's laugh is one voice locked across V01, V02 and D01. It must be generated, or performed by a consenting fictional-cast performer. No real person's voice is cloned, and no one's availability or permission is claimed.
There is no child in the script. No one is flagged for visible difference, religious dress, pregnancy or age 70+ (DRIVER's target is 61). Mental health is flagged for human review in the blockers.

Taste notes. 'Hands before faces': VENUS's left-thumb nick and right-hand scar, and JEAN's neck mole, hold identity before either face appears. 'Restraint over explanation': no knowing look to the lens, no menace register, and the organiser played flat. 'Dry over sentimental': her verdicts and 'J. Stay for breakfast.' are at one dry pitch. Casting breaks no note on purpose; S01's face break was already accepted upstream.
If D01 is ever produced live-action rather than generated (A09), the bedroom scenes need an intimacy coordinator and every performer's written consent. No performer is attached now.

blockers.issue: No market alcohol code was given, and the bar, the drinks and the tin put every visible adult under the alcohol rule.
blockers.resolution: Confirm the target markets. Until then the cast assumes a minimum of 25, and every visible face, bar background included, reads 30+. If any market sets a higher minimum or bans showing people drinking, re-age the cast or recut the bar scenes and S03.

blockers.issue: The script pairs a killer with psychiatric medication she hasn't taken in weeks, and Lucas framed it as mental health. That is the representation risk the must-avoid names (meds treated as the explanation for the killings), and the craft brief flags disability, which can include mental illness, for human review.
blockers.resolution: Get human or sensitivity review of SC15 and of D01's framing of her meds before the pitch pieces circulate. Casting holds the organiser beat to the padlock-check register (no wince, no tremor, no pause on the label) and never ties her performance to a diagnosis. The reviewer confirms this or asks for changes.

blockers.issue: Heritage for all four characters is a casting choice, not a script requirement, and the setting is unconfirmed (US assumed; the Raptors shirt points to Toronto). The circulating pieces raise the stakes: S01 and V02 make a dead Black man the key image beside a laughing woman, and they travel without D01's context.
blockers.resolution: Lucas approves or reassigns with S01 and V02 roughs in front of him, not from this text alone. If anything changes, redo skin hex, hair texture and JEAN's dead-state notes together, keep VENUS and JEAN matched or say why not, and restate the heritages for the confirmed country.

blockers.issue: JEAN's anchors depend on the A16 test. In a moving convertible a still, open-eyed passenger must hold his identity, his dead eyes (upper lid at the top edge of the iris, a dry grey-filmed cornea, dusted lashes) and a set neck that doesn't bob. B07 and V02-B04 also prove death with 'the wind moves his hair', which an 8-10 cm tight 4A top may not show.
blockers.responsible_agent: Director / generation lead, with the stylist
blockers.resolution: Run the 5 s A16 test on these anchors before locking them. Check that the top of his hair visibly moves in the wind within the 5 s; if it doesn't, the stylist loosens or lengthens it. If the pallor or the dry cornea doesn't read, carry the death through dust, unblinking eyes and a desaturated grade, never a lighter hex, and use the parked-car fallback.

evidence.specificity: All six notes from the last round were addressed, and each fix gives the stylist and the director something they can act on. Quoted line: "Dead eyes (V01-B07, B08, V02-B04 to B06, SC18): the upper lid rests at the top edge of the iris in every shot; the cornea is dry and dulled with a faint grey film and no wet shine; dust sits on the lashes." The height ladder is exact and checks out: "177 cm: 7 cm shorter than JEAN, 7 cm taller than BARTENDER" (184 / 180 / 177 / 170). The registers without the laugh are playable: "SC15, the organiser gets the same face and hands as the padlock check (V01-B10). She opens one lid, looks and closes it, with no wince, no tremor and no pause on the turned label." One follow-up question is still open for makeup: what his face looks like after lying face-down all night (note 1).
evidence.distinctiveness: Several details could only come from this idea. Quoted: "Beside the dead JEAN she blinks normally, so in a shared frame her blink is the one difference between them." The repeated gesture now ties the route to the plot: "a digit rests, then slides off. Her thumb does it on the flip icon; her fingertip does it on the chimney straw and on the tin... SC18 is the first time she presses." The left-thumb nick "reads nail-side over the screen UI", and it carries the route's emotional promise. What holds the score at 8 is VENUS's face line, which is the craft brief's calibration example carried over: "[micro] Long face, narrow jaw, heavy straight brows with the right one 3 mm higher". Also, all four characters have heavy brows.
evidence.fit: The route's payoff (A06) is now locked in performance: "Lens rule: her eyes never go into any lens... The first time is SC18, when she looks into her own front camera while his eyes aim past it." The must-avoid on meds is kept, with the organiser played at the padlock register and a sensitivity-review blocker. The morning after follows ref 06: "She lies still, a hand to her forehead, eyes on the back of his head, not the ceiling." Lucas's 'pale' is treated with care: "never lightened... so the generator doesn't lighten a Black man's skin to signal death." The heritage blocker now sends the decision to Lucas "with S01 and V02 roughs in front of him", and the setting (US or Toronto) is recorded as an assumption. The bible respects every must-avoid, uses no real likeness, and 'female Dexter' does not appear.
evidence.craft: The continuity logic is now sound: "Rigor is a timeline assumption, not a medical claim... his neck is played as set from V01 through SC18: no bob, and the head gives only a few degrees with the shoulders." It explains why his eyes miss both her and the front camera, and the SC17 dressing conflict is flagged to the director and writer. The mole and the receding left temple are placed on the side the camera actually sees in a left-hand-drive car. The anchors are tagged, with two macro anchors per character and one unique trait each. Two things hold it at 8. First, the post-mortem reasoning stops at rigor: SC16 leaves him face-down all night, which runs against 'pale' in the one face shot, and nothing records that choice. Second, one consent has no owner or status: "It must be generated, or performed by a consenting fictional-cast performer."

notes.target: JEAN.visual_identity_anchors (dead-state skin) and assumptions (rigor line)
notes.note: The bible now works from a post-mortem timeline, but it stops at rigor. SC16 leaves him face-down "where he has lain since the night", so by the dusk face shot (B07) blood would have pooled and settled in his face and neck, which reads as the opposite of Lucas's 'pale'. Add one assumption next to the rigor line: lividity is deliberately not shown. The dead state stays 'the same hex desaturated, grey-ash at the lips, lids and under the eyes', and neither makeup nor the generator may darken or mottle the face. Flag it to the director and writer in the same line as the rigor note. Describe no discoloration, bruising or wound.
notes.source: Quality bar, craft (nothing physically implausible; continuity holds); must-include 'his pale, lost eyes'; must-avoid gore; brief (pitch pieces must circulate)

notes.target: assumptions (VENUS's laugh voice; the live-action contingency)
notes.note: Write each consent in the bar's form. For VENUS's laugh: source, this bible; scope, V01, V02, D01 and any cut made from them; owner, the producer; status, pending, with no performer, voice model or consent attached or claimed. Do the same for the live-action line (intimacy coordinator and written performer consent for the SC07 insert and SC14-SC16), with the producer as owner and status pending. Add one check before anything circulates: the generation lead compares every generated face against real people, and the producer signs off, status pending.
notes.source: Quality bar, craft ('Every right and consent the work needs is named with its source, scope and owner and left pending for the producer'); rules (never use a real person's likeness)

notes.target: VENUS.visual_identity_anchors, the [micro] face line
notes.note: This face is the craft brief's calibration example (ENID): long face, heavy straight brows with one 3 mm higher, and alongside it long limbs with shoulders narrower than hips and a pale scar at the thumb knuckle. All four characters also have heavy brows. Keep the build (it is Lucas's 'tall slim') and both hand marks (they belong to the flip icon and the chin touches). Rechoose the face so it is hers, for example 'medium-length face, narrow jaw, fine light brows set wide apart'. Let the three freckles on her left cheekbone carry the asymmetry, which also sets her apart from JEAN's 'heavy low brows that almost meet'.
notes.source: Craft brief ('If a profile could drop into any brand's spot... it is not finished'; the weak/strong example is 'for calibration only'); distinctiveness criterion

notes.target: blockers (mental-health issue) and JEAN.role_in_story (heritage sentence)
notes.note: 'The script pairs a killer with psychiatric medication' names a drug class that the verified facts ('Her meds are in her bathroom', 'She hasn't taken the meds in weeks') do not give and the script withholds ('No drug name, no diagnosis'). Rewrite it as 'medication Lucas tied to mental health ("play into mental health")', labelled as his framing. In JEAN's heritage, 'Because heritage is not prompted, it cannot show in his face. He is Black like VENUS' reads as a contradiction. Rewrite: 'The Haitian-American label is recorded and not prompted, so it can't show; what reads on screen is his skin hex and hair texture, matched to VENUS so the killing doesn't read as a cross-racial story.'
notes.source: Rules (label anything beyond the verified facts as an assumption); must-avoid (meds as the explanation); craft brief (record heritage in role_in_story, never in an anchor)

notes.target: DRIVER.visual_identity_anchors (right-hand [macro])
notes.note: 'Raised veins and brown age spots' will not resolve at dash-cam resolution, so they cannot be macro. Keep '[macro] long, bony right hand with swollen knuckles, rising into the dome light' and move the veins and age spots to a micro anchor, or drop them.
notes.source: Craft brief (tag each anchor macro, meaning it reads in the widest shot, or micro, meaning close-up)

notes.target: JEAN.performance_style (SC15)
notes.note: 'Recorded wild' is a sound-department decision. Keep what he performs ('breathing only: slow and loud, one long stop, then a rasp; face down, no lip-sync') and cut the recording method.
notes.source: Judging instruction (detail that does a later department's job is scope creep and costs craft)

locations.description: Venus's car, a vintage open two-seater roadster with a 1950s shape (A11). In SC04 the black canvas top is up and it is parked across from the bar at night. In SC01-SC02 (V01-B01 to B11, V02, S01) the top is down. It must not look like any real make: long bonnet, rounded wings, low cut-down doors, a plain oval grille with 6 horizontal bars, round lamps, no bonnet ornament, badge holes filled, plain body-colour hubcaps. US, 2026 ASSUMED. It is left-hand drive, so Venus drives on the left and Jean sits on the right with his head to the passenger door. It has a rear plate only (a rear-plate-only state, ASSUMED), and the plate is blank in every shot. She has owned the car for years ASSUMED. The last thing she did before V01-B01 was seat Jean and put his sunglasses on him (SC17). Wear: the black steering-wheel rim is rubbed from #2E2A26 gloss to #5A4636 matte in two 8 cm arcs at 10 and 2 o'clock, where her hands go. The driver's left seat bolster is darkened to #B9A98C over 20 x 8 cm from getting in and out. Dust is set as states under PR-57: the car is clean in the city (SC04). From V01-B01 it carries a gold film, with one 25 cm wiped arc on the passenger side of the dash where her phone forearm rests. That arc is the scene's one real detail. Background: only the road and the scrub move, and there are no other cars. These must stay blank: the plate (no characters), the dash dials (tick marks only, no numerals or logo), the steering-wheel boss and the wing flanks.
