The anchor A/B is the driver-side end of the dash. x runs along A toward D (rearward) and y toward C, in cm. Bearing 0° = toward wall C, clockwise. Cabin 115 (x) x 125 (y). Seat cushions sit 30 cm above the floor and are 45 cm wide: the driver's is centred at y 32, the passenger's at y 93. Seat backs are at x 105, and the bone leather headrest pads top out 72 cm above the cushion. Jean's pose: cheek on the passenger headrest at x 108, y 100, face at bearing 0° (toward C, the door). Glovebox: on the passenger dash face at y 76-106, with a 30 x 14 cm drop-down lid hinged at the bottom, its lower edge 50 cm above the floor. She reaches it across Jean's knees (V01-B09). Boot: x 150-215, lid hinged at its front edge. It holds PR-05, PR-06, PR-07 and two PR-22 (V01-B11). SC04: top up, side curtains down, driver window open toward the bar. The car is parked on the far kerb with the driver side facing the bar at 14 m. SC01: the car heads north, so the low west sun is behind Venus (wall A) and Jean's face, turned to C (east), is in shade.

locations.description: SC01 (V01-B01 to B08, V02-B01 to B06, the light for S01). US Southwest high desert, 2026 ASSUMED, within a day's drive of the city. A dead crossroads town, empty for decades ASSUMED: one block of six single-storey stucco storefronts, windows boarded, fascias sanded blank. Beyond it, a two-lane blacktop runs north through scrub flats toward low hills. Right-hand traffic, with a faded double-yellow centre line and white edge lines. No other vehicle, person, animal or wire appears in any shot; only the scrub moves in the wind. Wear: crazed asphalt. The stop sign's face is sun-chalked from red to #B8453A, with its white letters intact. A sand drift lies across the northbound stop line, and no tyre crosses it until hers (PR-58). One real detail: the stop sign nobody else will ever reach (V01-B02).

The stop line is 1.2 m before the crossing, and PR-58 lies across it. PR-10 stands on the east shoulder 2.2 m off the edge line, the bottom of the sign 2.1 m above the road, facing south. With the car at the stop line, the sign stands about 3 m ahead and to the right of Jean's head, behind him in the phone frame. Beyond x 150: scrub flats, with hills 2-5 km to the east. The sun is low in the west, behind the driver; by V01-B05 it is blue dusk.

locations.description: SC02 (V01-B09 to B11). An abandoned US Southwest roadside motel, built about 1958 and shut about 25 years ago ASSUMED (ref 08 as the brief describes it): a two-storey stucco room block with a gutted upper floor, a single-storey office, a long carport, a peeling sign on steel legs and dry palms. Venus has used room 3 for weeks (LOC-04). History in objects: the office step's unbroken dust is her proof that nobody has come (V01-B10). Her own traffic has left one bare track, 40 cm wide, #A89878 packed against #B7A98C loose dust, running about 5 m from the carport bay to her door. Background: palm fronds and scrub move, and a loose sign panel ticks. The highway stays empty, with no vehicles or people.

locations.description: The motel room: SC03 (V01-B11 to B14, S02) and SC18. Room 3 of the 1958 block ASSUMED, shut about 25 years and stripped (no bed frame, no TV). Venus has used it on and off for about five weeks ASSUMED, counted by the nine emptied gallon jugs. It is where she builds the wall and brings each man afterwards (A14). Walls: the period motel finish, knotty-pine tongue-and-groove paneling in 15 cm vertical boards, aged to amber #7A5A3C under dull satin varnish; the pins go straight in. Outlets are two-slot, ungrounded NEMA 1-15 with brown bakelite plates, and dead; one plate is missing on wall B at y 120, 30 cm up. The last thing before V01-B12: she left days ago with the bedroll laid out and the wall up. locations.description: The dive bar and its street: seen from the car in SC04, then SC05 to SC08 and S03. A dive bar in an unnamed US Southwest city, 2026, open about 40 years ASSUMED. It is in a 1950s single-storey strip of painted brick #7E4B3A with a flat stucco parapet, with one fan palm in a sidewalk cut-out. The streetlights are LED cobra heads, so the only amber on the sidewalk is the bar's own window spill. Inside is a long, narrow regulars' room, going by refs 01-03 as the brief describes them: amber wall sconces, a red neon strip over the back bar, a green-glowing glass-front bottle fridge, candles in glasses on the counter, a chalkboard menu smudged past reading. It is Thursday and near empty: three patrons in silhouette at the far end and one bartender. It is Jean's third night on the same stool. Wear: the varnish is worn to raw #6B4A30 in a 40 x 25 cm patch at Jean's stool, from regulars' elbows. Dozens of faint dull rings #5A4030 mark the counter. The brass footrail is rubbed bright #C9A15A in front of each stool. Background: the patrons move slowly, stay lower in contrast than the straws and never cross the straw house or the candle. One real detail: PR-30 standing in candle wax.

locations.description: SC09. The rideshare's back seat, seen from a cabin-facing dash cam. A generic late-model mid-size sedan, dark grey #2F3236, with no badges and no rideshare stickers, logos or trade dress (A10). Background: cool LED streetlight slides across the side glass (no sodium, as in LOC-05), and nothing outside is legible. The cam cannot see the mirror's face, so the driver's watching reads as his own face at the lower edge of frame, eyes lifted to the mirror. One real detail: the dash cam, a second recording of Jean that Venus doesn't control.

locations.description: SC10. Venus's building: the lobby and the stairs up to her door. A renovated 1920s downtown mid-rise in the same unnamed US Southwest city, 2026 ASSUMED, where she has lived about two years ASSUMED. At night there is no doorman, and no residents are seen or heard. Honed white marble, satin brass, a quiet stair. Wear: the marble is polished to a gloss path 90 cm wide from the street door to the stair foot (#EDEAE4 gloss within #E9E6E0 honed). One real detail: the marble curtail step at the stair foot, rounded and projecting, the step she warns him about ('Mind the step').

locations.description: The white apartment: entry, living room and hall to the bedroom. SC10 (from the door), SC12-SC14 and SC17. This is her lure flat (A14), on the second floor, white on white; nothing sits on any surface unless a beat needs it. Kept about two years ASSUMED and cleaned daily. Before SC10 she vacuumed the rug, leaving fresh stripes, and filled the ice bucket. She missed the three drops at the bedroom threshold (PR-45), which belong to the previous man (A13). Wear, all of it marks of cleaning: 30 cm vacuum stripes on the rug, alternating matte and sheen. After SC17, the scrubbed 30 x 30 cm patch at the threshold is flatter and whiter (#F4F3EF matte) than the satin floor (#EFEDE8). A taste note is broken on purpose: there is no dish rack and no charging cable, because the tone makes tidiness the horror (the 'clean' tone line; ref 05 as the brief describes it). One real detail: Jean's shoes lined up on the white mat. Background: the sheer curtains hang still, and the city beyond shows no legible signage.

assumptions: Place and year: an unnamed US Southwest city, 2026 (ASSUMED), for the bar, the rideshare and the white apartment, within a day's drive of the desert road and the motel. The script runs on one continuous timeline: SC04 is Thursday night, and the drive is the next evening in the same car, fetched from outside the bar. The Canadian option is dropped. Details generators tend to mix up, now locked: right-hand traffic; left-hand-drive cars; a rear-plate-only state (ASSUMED) with every plate blank; English signage; a red octagon 'STOP'; NEMA 5-15 sockets in the 2026 apartment and lobby; two-slot, ungrounded NEMA 1-15 outlets in the 1958 motel room.

Street lighting: LED cobra heads (4000K ASSUMED), since most US cities have converted by 2026. No sodium fixture is written. The bar's own window spill carries the amber on the sidewalk, and the rideshare cabin gets cool LED slides (#B9C3CC).

All dimensions, ages and tenures are ASSUMED from the category, since none are verified: the car, the rooms, the tin, the printer, the prints, the 1958 motel build, about five weeks at the motel and about two years in the apartment.

Motel room finish: knotty-pine tongue-and-groove paneling, the period roadside-motel wall, replaces the earlier lime plaster. It takes the pins, and the paler rectangle on wall C is where the motel's own picture kept the pine from ambering.

Photo count: about 250 prints (ASSUMED), so the room meets the verified fact that the walls are covered in photos of the man, even though the script says 'dozens'. About 180 are on wall C and about 70 on wall B above the bedroll. Bare pine at x 280-345 on wall C stays empty until SC18, when the next man's prints and the photo of them together go up there.

The marks that show how long she has lived in the motel room now sit inside the held frame toward wall C: the jug row along wall D just past the door's sweep, the bedroll along wall B at y 190-400, the paler rectangle and the pin holes on wall C. The bags stay under the boarded window, out of that view.

White apartment: PR-44 moves to the table's north end so that SC12's fingertip on the tin and SC13's hand on her thigh can be staged. Her knees are about 35 cm from Jean's, and the tin sits between them at x 140, y 525.

Rideshare: they get in on the kerb side (right). Jean slides across first, so her tin pocket is on his side. The dome light is in the rear headliner, with a front master switch for the driver (ASSUMED).

Car: silver-grey paint with bone leather, so the REC dot stays the only red in the drive and the leather carries her white. The red car in ref 11 was the alternative and is rejected for that reason (upstream left the colour to production design).
Straws are plain white paper, so the house reads on the dark counter at 12:1. The tin is satin gunmetal, not bright steel, because bright steel on white gloss falls below 3:1.
The car heads north in SC01, so the low west sun sits behind Venus (the route puts the sun behind her) and Jean's turned face is in shade.

In LOC-04 the chairs stand side by side with their backs to the photo wall, facing the door. V01-B13 then reads as a table set for two, and the SC18 front-camera photo has Jean's wall behind both of them.
Dust is set-owned and tracked as states under PR-57: the dash, Jean's collar (agreed with the stylist) and the eyes (handed to makeup for V01-B07).

Legible text, written verbatim for compositing: the phone UI 'REC 00:00:04' through 'REC 01:05:00' as scripted; 'STOP'; 'MOTEL'; 'OFFICE'; 'NO FURTHER ACTION'; the dash-cam time '01:47:12' (ASSUMED, just after last call). Nothing else is legible.

Surfaces that must stay blank, because generators add fake logos: the car's grille, wings, wheels, dials and plate; the storefronts; the bottle labels, fridge, chalkboard, neon and coasters; the rideshare's badges and stickers; the dash cam; the mailboxes and door; the speaker, ice bucket and pedal bin; both phones; the organiser, vial and toilet paper; the cans, jugs and printer; the gas pump and courthouse in the prints; the T-shirt (stylist).

There is no product (route R2 stretch). Each product_placement field gives the device doing the job, its contrast and its clear zone instead. The taste note 'the product is a tool, then a hero' does not apply.

Taste notes: each location names its one real detail. Broken on purpose: the white apartment has no dish rack or charging cable, because its tidiness is the horror. Ref 06's patterned bedding is replaced with white to hold the colour theme.
The craft limit of about five locked props per frame is exceeded in V01-B13 and S02, because the script names more. LOC-04 gives a lock order.

References 01-11 were not inspected; there is no reference reader in this run. They are used only as the brief describes them, and no character or set is modelled on a real person or a real, recognisable place.

Camera, lenses and lighting are left to the DP. The only requests are the stylist's denim tone for the pistol grip, the tin's mirror path, and the dust hand-offs to the stylist and makeup. The 'planned held view' in LOC-04 says where the marks must be visible; it does not place the camera.

blockers.issue: The two-seater stays across from the bar after SC08, and SC17 ends with Jean in the white armchair. No beat covers her fetching the car or getting him down to it. The SC04 prints and report (PR-08, PR-09) sit on the passenger seat that Jean later occupies.

blockers.issue: SC11 has Jean wipe the rim and see faint pink on the tissue, but dry blood on glazed china flakes off brown. The pink needs a damp tissue, which is an action the script doesn't have.

blockers.issue: Clearance is pending for the original phone UI and the 'Naked and Famous' cocktail name, and there is a risk that a 1950s roadster silhouette reads as a real make's trade dress.
blockers.resolution: Everything is built unbranded, with a generic grille and filled badge holes. If the UI reads as a real OS, simplify it to the REC dot and timer, as the route states. Nothing is claimed as cleared.

evidence.specificity: All six notes from the last round were addressed. A crew or a generator can build almost every set from these numbers without asking. The drops are fixed by position, size, hex and contrast: "Threshold drops: three dried blood drops, 3, 4 and 5 mm across, dark matte crust #6E1C18 on the #EFEDE8 satin floor, 9.7:1" and "S1 SC10 to SC14: at x 575, 588 and 600, y 880, 886 and 883, just inside the threshold on the hall side." The stair arithmetic now works: "25 risers of 17.6 cm (4.40 m) and 28 cm treads. Flight 1, 13 risers, rises north along wall D at x 680-800, y 120-456" (12 treads x 28 = 336 cm, which is the stated run). Dust now has states: "Collar C2 V01-B02, not before B02: her hand has brushed the collar points back to #111111; dust is still on the shoulders." It falls short of 10 in three places. Most palettes cover only 75-92% of their frame. The PR-20 grid cannot hold "landscape and portrait mixed" at a 12 cm row pitch. PR-50 gives the next department nothing that shows "weeks" on screen.
evidence.distinctiveness: None of these objects could be moved into another project. The payoff print is designed to read by size alone: "It is the only card-size print on a wall of 15 x 10 cm prints, so it reads by its size with the sound off (A06)." The next man is planted in the motel's own history: "A paler 60 x 80 cm rectangle #A88458 on wall C at x 283-343, heights 155-235, where the motel's own picture hung for decades and the pine never ambered", which stays bare until SC18. Venus's care reads as a verdict: "S2 SC10: side by side on PR-40, toes toward the door, 2 cm apart, placed by Venus." The cleaning leaves its own mark: "a 30 x 30 cm patch flatter and whiter (#F4F3EF matte)". The stop sign that nobody else reaches has its proof too, in "two tyre tracks 16 cm wide... No other tracks." All of these serve R2's idea that she is trying to get into one photograph with him.
evidence.fit: Every must-include has a set, a prop and states keyed to the script's IDs, and every must-avoid is held. The verified fact about the wall is now true of the build: "about 250 gloss 15 x 10 cm long-lens prints of Jean... He is alone in every print, and none shows the two of them together (verified fact)." The meds follow the must-avoid: "Every compartment is full, with 2 plain white round 8 mm tablets, no imprint. Seen, never named (must avoid)." The method stays off screen: "The interior and contents are never framed." The place and timeline are locked to the script's one continuous timeline ("an unnamed US Southwest city, 2026 (ASSUMED)... The Canadian option is dropped"). The broken taste note is flagged: "there is no dish rack and no charging cable, because the tone makes tidiness the horror". Rights are left pending with named owners: "Clearance is pending for the original phone UI and the 'Naked and Famous' cocktail name... Nothing is claimed as cleared." One gap: the fact "She hasn't taken the meds in weeks" has nothing in the frame to carry the 'weeks' (note 2).
evidence.craft: The previous round's physical slips are fixed and I checked the numbers. The motel rooms now fit ("12 ground-floor rooms 3.6 m wide... Her room is the third, at x 23.2-26.8"). The straw sits at the right height ("top about 11 cm above the rim"). The portrait print fits its span ("at x 305-315"). Jean's phone is distinct ("A spiderweb crack runs across the top-right third of the screen"). The damp tissue is stated and flagged to the writer. The contrast claims hold when recomputed: "Gunmetal #4A4D52 on white gloss #F7F6F3 gives 7.8:1" (about 7.85), the lifted lid at 4.7:1, the grip on #8FA3B8 denim at 5.5:1, the straws at 12:1 and the collar at 11.8:1. The chairs now touch without overlapping ("moved to x 165, its seat edge touching PR-19's"). It is still an 8, not a 9. The new armchair sits on Jean's legs ("Jean sits at its north end, y 540-590" against "PR-44 stands at the table's north end, x 110-190, y 555-635"). The car's front is detailed but the rear, which the planned views actually see, is not. The palettes don't add up to their frames. Two rooms disagree on compass bearings. A senior production designer would send this with those small notes.

notes.target: PR-50 states S1-S3 · LOC-09 (SC15)
notes.note: 'Every compartment is full' looks the same as 'filled this morning'. With the day letters rightly removed, the lid she opens at row 1, column 1 no longer reads as the first day. So nothing in the frame carries the verified 'weeks'. Give the organiser a sign of time that uses no text, and key it as states. Suggested: echo PR-14 with an even, unbroken dust film on the glass shelf and the lids (give the hex and finish), the only dust in the flat. When she lifts the organiser in S2 it leaves a clean 22 x 12 cm rectangle, and S3 puts it back inside that rectangle. The alternative is raised tactile dots on the lids, one to seven per column, so the lid she opens reads as day one. Keep: no drug name, the label turned to the wall, and nothing that offers the meds as the reason for the killings.
notes.source: Verified fact: 'She hasn't taken the meds in weeks.' Must-include: 'Her meds, untaken for weeks'. Craft brief: 'Every set has a history told by objects... shown by a prop or a state.' Must-avoid: meds as the explanation.

notes.target: LOC-01 description · the car's exterior
notes.note: The only exterior detail specified is the front, 'a plain oval grille with 6 horizontal bars', which no planned view sees. In V01-B09 the car noses into the carport facing 0°. B11 is at the boot. SC04 shows the driver side, S01 is from behind her shoulder, and ref 09 is 'seen from behind'. An oval horizontal-bar mouth on a long-bonnet two-seater with cut-down doors is also the signature face of real 1950s British roadsters: the look-alike trade dress your own blocker warns about. Replace it with a small plain body-colour intake with no bars and no surround. Specify the rear to the same standard: tail-lamp form and size, bumper (a thin painted blade or none), the boot lid's shape and hinge line, the blank plate's position and its lamp, a plain filler cap and the exhaust exit. No fins, no chrome script, no badge. In the same entry, SC04's 'side curtains down, driver window open' reads both ways. State whether side screens are fitted with the driver's sliding panel open, or whether there are none.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Put marks where a planned view sees them'; 'No third-party logos, readable packaging or look-alike trade dress.' A10. Script V01-B09, B11; brief S01.

notes.target: Palettes · LOC-01, LOC-02, LOC-03, LOC-04, LOC-05, LOC-06, LOC-07, LOC-09, LOC-10
notes.note: Most palettes don't account for the frame they describe. The totals are: LOC-05 75%, LOC-01 80%, LOC-04 85%, LOC-09 86%, LOC-06, LOC-07 and LOC-10 87%, LOC-03 92%. LOC-02 lists both skies at 24% in one list, which comes to 115%. Name each palette's master view, as LOC-04 does with 'S02 master', and bring each one to 100%. For LOC-04 the missing 15% is presumably the lantern-dark shadow plus the bedroll and jug corner. LOC-05's missing quarter is the blanked bottle wall, the booths and the window. Split LOC-02 into a V01-B01-B04 palette and a B05-B08 palette. Give LOC-01 its V01 phone-frame master, since the desert behind Jean is most of that frame.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Each entry is a hex, a role... and its share of the master view.' What a creative director rejects: 'shares no frame could produce'.

notes.target: PR-20 grid · LOC-07/LOC-08-10 bearings · LOC-03 boot distance
notes.note: Three small fixes. (a) PR-20 says 'landscape and portrait mixed', but a 15 cm-tall portrait print can't sit in a 12 cm row pitch. Make wall C all landscape (15 x 12 = 180 at 17.5 x 12 cm, unchanged). Make wall B all portrait at a 12 x 17 cm pitch: 14 x 5 = 70 over y 205-373, heights 150-235. The count stays at 250. (b) LOC-07 puts PR-39 'on the landing's east side, facing 270°', so you walk east into the flat. LOC-08 calls its entrance wall 'A (south)', and LOC-09 and LOC-10 inherit that. In building terms, LOC-10's wall D window, the SC16 morning light, faces south, not east. Relabel the compass words in LOC-08 to LOC-10, or turn the landing door so the two agree. (c) LOC-03 says 'the boot is 5 m from the door', but the coordinates (boot at about x 21.8, y 13.5; door at about x 26.1, y 18) give about 6.2 m. Fix the text or move the car one bay east.
notes.source: Quality bar, craft: 'continuity that holds', 'every cross-reference... is right'. Craft brief: 'Lock place and year'; 'Space is a plan with numbers'.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat B07 (42.0-50.0): close on her right hand turning his chin; his open eyes are the one face shot. Across the scene she wants him to look back at her. Two things stop her: he is dead, and she won't turn the lens on herself. B01 (0-4): she wants to wake him to the drive. She laughs loud on the mic, the way you laugh at a lover sleeping through the best part, and the frame jolts. B02 (4-10): she wants to make him presentable. She comes to a full stop at a sign nobody else will reach, 50 cm short of the untouched sand drift (PR-58), brushes the dust off him and straightens his collar. Her hand rests there a beat before she pulls away. Real detail: she obeys the stop line on an empty road and still finishes dressing him. B03 (10-18): hold. She keeps filming across three jumps and he never moves; the joke is that the pose never changes. B04 (18-26): she wants into the picture. Her thumb rests 2.2 s on the flip icon, played as shyness: a lover who won't appear in her own home video. It slides off and she laughs. B05 (26-34): she wants to keep seeing him as the light goes. Her index finger presses the phone's side button and the video light comes on him. B06 (34-42): the first time we see her face. She laughs at the wheel with her eyes on him, not the road. No knowing look, no lip bite, and her eyes never go to any lens. B07: she wants him to look at her, and the dark is her excuse to take off the sunglasses. Her laugh stops and she holds his chin 1-2 s. This is not shock; she already knows. B08 (50-56): she goes back behind the lens. She takes his sunglasses to herself, laughs more softly, and rests her thumb only 1.2 s ('not like this, not yet'). JEAN is absolutely still: no blink, no breath, and rigor has set his neck.
scenes.blocking: LOC-01 in LOC-02 with the top down, travelling north in the northbound lane. The low sun is in the west, behind the driver's side. VENUS sits in the driver seat (y 32), left hand on the wheel in the worn 10 o'clock arc. PR-01 is upright in her right hand at arm's length, just west of Jean's left shoulder, lens aimed east across it, so the east-side storefronts (PR-11) and the stop sign (PR-10, east shoulder) sit behind his head. JEAN has his cheek on the passenger headrest (x 108, y 100) and his face to the passenger door (east), PR-04 on. The lens sees only his collar, left jaw, left sunglasses arm and neck mole. The wind is relative, nose to tail. B02: front tyres stop 50 cm short of PR-58, with PR-10 about 3 m ahead and east of his head. Line of action: the road, with the car always heading north. Every full-width setup stays west of the car's centreline. B06 and B07 up to 45.0 are on the driver's (west) side: she is nearest the lens and he shows only the back of his head and the glasses. From 45.0 the B07 axis sits ahead of the windscreen, on or just west of the centreline, looking back south along the road. The chin turn brings his face from east to north-east, up the road's east verge, 45° off the door. From this axis it reads as a three-quarter with both eyes. His gaze runs past the lens on its east side and never reaches her. Rigor holds that set for the rest of V01 and SC18. B08: her right hand holds the phone forward of his face on the windscreen side, a hand's width west of his gaze line, lens aimed back at his eyes, so they sit centred in frame and aim past the lens. For 9:16: the phone-frame shots are natively upright. In B07, her hand and his face stay inside the middle third on both axes, because V02-B03 uses 42.8-43.8 and 45.0-46.0. Her face may fall outside it.
scenes.action_progression: Entry at 0.0: PR-01 recording with the light off, collar in state C1, dash in D2, PR-04 on him. Left hand on the wheel, right hand on the phone. B01, 0.0-4.0, one plate: hold on collar and jaw (1.8); a full-torso laugh jolts the frame (1.6); frame settles (0.6). B02, 4.0-10.0: the car rolls to a full stop and the frame dips (0.8); her left hand leaves the wheel and enters under the lens (0.7); two strokes brush the shoulder and collar points back to black, C1 to C2 (1.2); she pinches the left collar point flat (1.0); her hand rests on the collar (0.8); hidden cut at 8.9 as the withdrawing hand wipes the lens (0.4); the frame lurches as she pulls away over PR-58 (1.1). Plates: 4.0-8.9 and 8.9-10.0. Left hand back on the wheel. B03, 10.0-18.0, three plates: 10.0-12.6 storefronts (a second pass through the block), 12.6-15.3 open desert, 15.3-18.0 scrub hills. The head pose is identical in all three, the dust builds toward C3, and each cut lands on a snatch of laugh. B04, 18.0-26.0: hold (0.8); right thumb slides onto the flip icon (1.0); rests (2.2); slides back to the frame edge (0.8); laugh jolt at 22.8, with the plate join at 22.9 hidden in its blur; laugh (2.0); frame settles on him (1.2). Plates: 18.0-22.9 and 22.9-26.0. B05, 26.0-34.0: dusk, noisy picture (2.7); her right index finger presses PR-01's side button, off picture because the picture is the rear lens (0.3); at 29.0 the video light comes on and the plate join hides in the exposure pop; C3 dust glints as the car vibrates (5.0). Plates: 26.0-29.0 and 29.0-34.0. B06, 34.0-42.0: the frame tips toward her lap in a short, mostly blurred plate (0.8); the pillars open to full width (0.6); the phone lies face up in her lap, still recording with the light on; her right hand rests on her thigh; she laughs at the wheel with her eyes on him (6.6). Cut at 39.8, inside the laugh. B07, 42.0-50.0, plate 1 on the west side: her right hand goes from her lap to his face (0.8); lifts PR-04 off by the left arm, clear of his right ear (1.2); drops to his jaw with the glasses held open in her palm (1.0). Cut on action at 45.0 to the front axis as two fingers meet his chin. She turns it: the head gives a few degrees, the shoulders follow, and his face stops pointing north-east with no loll (1.4). Hold on the open eyes, hair moving, no blink (3.6). Her left hand stays on the wheel throughout. B08, 50.0-56.0: her right hand hooks the open left arm of PR-04 into her neckline at centre, lenses out (1.0); lifts PR-01 from her lap (1.0); the frame closes to upright (0.4); inside it his eyes are centred under the light and the frame shakes as she laughs (1.0); thumb to the icon (0.8), rests (1.2), slides back (0.6). Plates: 50.0-52.4 full width on the front axis, and 52.4-56.0 phone frame, generated long for V02.
scenes.emotional_shift: Hers. Before (B01-B06): laughing, filming, eyes on him. Trigger (B07), which the camera sees: she turns his chin and his open eyes land aimed north-east, past the lens and never at her. After: no laugh for 8 s, and her fingers stay on his chin a beat. In B08 she takes his sunglasses to herself and goes back behind the lens. The laugh returns softer and the thumb rest is shorter (1.2 s against 2.2 s), so the same gesture now reads 'not like this, not yet'. B04's rest is a hold: no trigger, same state, shyness. Up to B07, the viewer's shift from lover to dead man is carried by his stillness, not by any change in her.
scenes.transition_in: The pilot opens with no fade: from black straight into the phone's upright frame at REC 00:00:04. Her laugh and the wind on the mic start on frame one.
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut with a time jump to last light. B08's phone frame (thumb leaving the icon, wind on the mic) cuts to B09's locked-off carport at full width. The mic wind cuts dead and the cooling engine's ping starts on the cut. The eye goes from his eyes at the centre of the upright frame to the car under the MOTEL sign at centre.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' B04 and B08 carry it: twice, her right thumb rests on the flip-camera icon over him, then slides back. Cut this and the viewer loses the want: a woman films a man for an hour and can't turn the lens round. Without it, the wall, the table for two and SC18's press read as a collector's trophies.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Phone UI (REC dot, timer, flip icon), B01-B05 and B08. Method: composite in finishing over G plates; original design, clearance pending (A10). Acceptance: the timer reads 00:00:04, 00:06:12, 00:21:40, 00:38:15, 00:52:30, 00:53:10, 00:58:40 and 01:04:55, runs continuously within each beat, and shows no OS or maker marks. The video light is switched by PR-01's side button in B05, off picture, so no UI element changes state before SC18. Risk: generated digits or icons come out garbled.

Thumb on the icon (B04, B08; V02-B06). Method: a practical plate of a hand double's right thumb over a blank phone on green, composited over G. Acceptance: the thumb enters nail-side, rests 2.2 s (B04) or 1.2 s (B08) without a twitch, and never presses, so the UI never changes state. Risk: a generated thumb presses or morphs and spends SC18's payoff. Fallback: the script's under-a-second front-camera flip, with her eyes on him and never in the lens.

Collar touch, B02 (V02-B01). Method: G; the hand is risky. Acceptance: one hand, two strokes; the collar points go from dusted to #111111 while the shoulders keep their film (C1 to C2); his head does not move under her touch. Risk: extra fingers, or a nod that reads alive. Fallback: her hand rests on his collar with no adjusting.

Dead eyes, B07-B08 (V02-B04/B05). Method: G, locked in composite. Acceptance: zero blinks and zero eye movement across 45.0-50.0 and 52.4-56.0; upper lids at the top edge of the iris; dry, dulled corneas with dust on the lashes; gaze aimed north-east, past the lens on its east side; hair moving while the eyes hold. If a take fails, freeze the eye region from the best frame and keep the hair and background live. Risk: one blink kills the reveal. A16: first try in the moving car. The fallback is parked at the motel, where the wind comes from the highway (south) and lifts his hair toward the windscreen; don't match it to the moving plates.

Axis change at 45.0, from the west side to ahead of the windscreen. Acceptance: both setups sit west of the car's centreline, Venus is nearer the lens in both, and his face in the front-axis plate reads as a three-quarter with both eyes, not a profile. Risk: a setup east of the centreline crosses the line and puts his gaze into the lens.

Three-step hand chains, B07 (lift the glasses, hold them open, turn the chin) and B08 (hook the glasses, lift the phone, thumb). Method: G; hands risky. Acceptance: PR-04 stays in her right hand across the 45.0 cut and is hooked, lenses out, by 51.0; it never vanishes or doubles. Fallback: it is already hooked at 50.0, cut on the lift.

Vehicle. Method: G. Acceptance: one open two-seater with a 1950s shape, left-hand drive, a blank rear plate, no badges and no numerals on the dials, travelling north in the right-hand lane; no other vehicle, person or animal in any frame. Risk: a real make's grille or a badge (A10).

Jump-cut registration, B03. Method: one locked G of Jean over varied background plates. Acceptance: head, collar and sunglasses overlay within a few pixels across all three; only the sun's height and the background change.
PR-10 'STOP': composite the letters if the generator distorts them. No other legible text in LOC-02.
Laugh sync, B06, the only sync in V01. Acceptance: laugh audio peaks align with the visible torso shakes within 2 frames. One laugh voice is locked across V01, V02 and D01.
Hair in wind: hers is held (stylist) and never falls over the hand shots. His top hair must move in B07: it is the life in the frame that the eyes don't have.
No slow motion anywhere; the laugh, the drive and the eyes all play at 24 fps real speed (taste note).

S01 comes from this scene's gold light, before B04. Stage it from behind her right shoulder: the phone in her right hand shows Jean under the REC dot, the real Jean sits beside it with his head to the door, and she laughs in three-quarter profile, eyes on him, never the lens. It breaks 'hands before faces' on purpose, as the script decided: a poster needs its lead.
Frame open and close (B06, B08): a graphic transition built in finishing. The pillars open in 0.6 s and close in 0.4 s, riding the phone's own motion. No dissolve.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat B10: close on the unbroken dust as she leans over the office step to tug the padlock rather than set a foot in it. She wants proof that nobody has found the motel, and she can't bring him in until she has it. B09 (56-60): she arms herself. She leans across his knees to the glovebox and takes the pistol by the grip, keeping the muzzle down and away from him the whole time. Real detail: trained handling, even beside a dead man. She seats it grip-up in her right back pocket. B10 (60-64): she checks. She walks the frontage alone, glances once at the empty highway, leans over the step and tugs the padlock twice, then looks down at the dust. B11 (64-72): she moves in. She unloads fast with both arms full, in one trip, and doesn't look back at him. She shoulders the swollen door. JEAN is still, his head where B07 left it.
scenes.blocking: LOC-03 at last light. The wind comes from the highway (south), and the fronds lean toward the room block. The car is nosed in facing north in the carport at x 21.0-22.55, y 13.5-17.5, its passenger side (Jean) toward room 3's door PR-15 (x 25.7-26.6) and the boot at the south end. B09: she leans east across Jean's knees to the glovebox (passenger dash, y 76-106). The lid drops and stays open. B10: from the driver's side she walks west along the frontage to the office door (x 12, south face) and stops on the gravel at the east end of PR-14, toes off the step. scenes.action_progression: B09, 56.0-60.0, one plate: hold on the engine ping (0.4); she leans across his knees, right hand to the glovebox (0.9); thumbs the latch and the lid drops (0.4); lifts PR-02 out by the grip, muzzle down (0.7); sits back upright (0.8); lifts her right hip and slides the pistol grip-up into her right back pocket, 6 cm showing (0.8). Hard cut; the walk back is elided. B11, 64.0-72.0. scenes.emotional_shift: Before: quick and armed, with one glance at the highway during the walk. Trigger: the unbroken dust on PR-14, which the camera sees. After: she turns back without another look at the road and unloads at speed, both shoulders loaded. She checks nothing else for the rest of the cold open.
scenes.transition_in: Hard cut with a time jump from SC01's phone frame to the full-width carport. The cooling-engine ping replaces the mic wind.
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut on the door scraping open: from her back going into the dark doorway, eye at centre, to inside the black room, where the lantern click lights the wall (SC03). The scrape carries over the cut, and the wind in the palms becomes wind at the door.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' B11 carries it: she carries his bag beside hers into the room, moving in with him rather than stashing a body. Cut this and the viewer loses that the motel is a home she has kept and checked for the two of them. The pistol and the untouched dust are her guarding it; without them the room reads as a lair for trophies instead of a house for two.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Pistol PR-02, B09-B10. Method: G, or a practical plate if the generator can't hold its shape. Acceptance: the muzzle never crosses Jean or the lens; grip up with 6 cm showing in the right back pocket, readable against light-wash denim (the world bible asks the stylist for #8FA3B8); no markings. Risk: a morphing or camera-pointed gun reads as femme-fatale gloss. Fallback: already in the pocket, no hand on it.
Leaning over a dead body, B09, a five-step chain. Acceptance: Jean's knees and head do not move while she leans across him. Risk: he shifts and reads alive.
PR-14 dust. Acceptance: no footprint on the step in any frame of B10 or later.
Carry, B11. Method: G. Acceptance: two shoulder bags and two sacks, with nothing appearing or vanishing across the 68.0 cut. The two full jugs ride inside sack 2 (see blockers).
PR-12: 'MOTEL' and 'OFFICE' verbatim, composited if garbled; no other text. The loose panel may move and tick.
Door, B11. Method: G. Acceptance: two shoves and one stop at 35°, not a single swing.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on her hands and the chair legs as she pulls the second chair up to the table and sets it square beside hers. She wants the table set for two. We play her hands; her head stays above the lantern's pool and never turns to the door (taste note: hands before faces). She unpacks fast, in pairs and handfuls, like someone who has done it many times. She gives one look, to the empty boards beside her own chair, and slows only for the chair. Then she leaves to bring him in. The held frame has nobody in it.
scenes.blocking: LOC-04. The camera is near the door (wall A) facing north toward wall C, the planned B13/S02 view; exact placement is the DP's. PR-15 stands open at 90° behind camera. She works from the table's east end (about x 245, y 365), facing west, so the tabletop and wall C stay clear. PR-16 is already on the table, off, at x 180, y 365. Placements: PR-24 at x 130-160, y 340-360; PR-21 in two stacks at x 182-198, y 382-397; PR-22 at x 206-238, y 382-397; PR-25 at x 200, y 340, slot facing south. The bare pine on wall C at x 280-345 stays empty.

Hard cut. scenes.emotional_shift: Before: fast unpacking, her hands never pause. Trigger, which the camera sees: as she sets the printer, her head turns to the bare boards beside PR-18, the one empty place at the table. After: her hands slow. The chair gets 3.3 s against 1.8 s for six cans: two hands to square it, one nudge, and both hands resting on its back for 0.7 s, the only rest in the scene, before she goes for him. B13-B14 are a hold: nobody is in frame, and the room carries it.
scenes.transition_in: Hard cut from SC02's doorway into the dark room; the door scrape carries across. The lantern click reveals the room.
scenes.transition_out: V01: the LIMERENCE card sits on the held frame in silence, then cut to black at 90.0. In the pilot: a hard cut from the card's silence to SC04's upright phone frame. Nothing matches across the cut; instead SC04's first frame echoes V01-B01's collar-and-jaw framing, with Jean alive.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' PR-20 over the table carries it, with PR-19 pulled up beside PR-18: a wall of him alone, none of them together, above a table set for two. Cut this and the viewer loses the gap the idea lives in, hundreds of photos and not one of her with him, and the printer (PR-25) that SC18 pays off.
practical_or_compositing_flags: PR-20 wall (verified fact: none of them together). Method: composite. Generate or shoot about 40 unique long-lens images of the locked JEAN (a bar window, an unbranded gas pump, crossing a street; half night, half day; always in black), then tile them to about 250 prints as a CG texture on the pine. Acceptance at S02 resolution: no print contains a second person or any woman; no legible text; Jean in black in every print; the pine at x 280-345 left bare. Risk: a freely generated wall invents couple photos and breaks the fact.

Held frame, B13-B14 and S02. Method: lock one frame and hold it as a still; the lantern runs on batteries, so nothing flickers. Acceptance: zero pixel motion from 82.0 to 90.0 (a flat difference matte). Risk: generator drift, floating dust or breathing light.

Hands unpacking. Method: G across two 5 s plates, many objects. Acceptance: the counts hold (6 cans, 2 full jugs, 5 oranges, 1 printer, 9 empty jugs by the door), and nothing appears on the table without a hand placing it. Risk: a hand merges with a can or jug.
Head turn at the printer. Acceptance: it reads in silhouette against the lit wall, her face never lit and never toward the lens.
Chair. Acceptance: PR-19 ends square beside PR-18 with the seat edges level and the backs below the photos' 95 cm bottom edge; the drag is visibly slower than the unpacking.
Title: LIMERENCE only, final 2 s, silent, composited. S02 is the B13 frame, with no text.

After: her laugh shakes the frame while his eyes stay still (B05), and the thumb rests and retreats (B06). With the sound off, the timer and the unblinking eyes carry time and death, and the thumb carries the want.
scenes.transition_in: It opens straight on the phone frame mid-action at the collar, with wind on the mic from frame one.

scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' B06 carries it: her thumb on the flip icon over his open eyes, sliding back. Cut it and V02 becomes a dead-body reveal; the want, and the reason to open V01, are gone.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Footage length. V01-B08's phone section runs 3.6 s, but V02-B04 to B06 need about 7 s on his eyes. Method: generate the B08 eyes plate with handles (two plates of up to 5 s joined on a laugh jolt) and shoot the thumb plate long. Acceptance: no frame is used twice in V02.
Muted read. Acceptance: shown with the sound off, a test viewer reads 'a man who never wakes, and she won't turn the camera on herself'. The REC timer is the only on-screen text besides the title.
Push-in resolution: generate the eyes plate at 4K equivalent so the B04 push keeps the dull corneas and the dust on the lashes.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on her hands as the pistol goes into the glovebox and the tin comes out. She wants to go in before he leaves alone again, and walking into his frame means going without the gun. Tactic 1: from the collar-and-jaw framing of V01-B01, she zooms to his face until the lens runs out and the picture breaks into grain, and keeps it there. Real detail: she would rather have his face soft than the room sharp. Tactic 2: she waits while he raises two fingers for another. Trigger: the BARTENDER flicks the tab slip face-down in front of him, and she moves at once. Jean's living face stays soft and grainy inside her phone, a picture rather than a performance shot.
scenes.blocking: LOC-01 with the top up and side curtains down, parked on the far kerb with the driver side to the bar at 14 m and the driver window open. VENUS is in the driver seat, PR-01 upright in her right hand at the window, PR-02 grip-up in her right back pocket. PR-08 (band on) lies on the passenger cushion with PR-09 half under it; PR-03 is closed in the glovebox. Through the window (LOC-05 wall A, x 40-440): JEAN on stool 2 (y 350), PR-33 at x 148, y 395, the BARTENDER in the aisle. After the trade she gets out of the driver door, on the street side facing the bar, and crosses to the glazed door (x 470-560).
scenes.action_progression: It opens inside her upright phone frame on his black collar and jaw through the glass, V01-B01's framing, with him alive and lifting his glass (2.0). Her right fingertip lifts, and her right thumb raises the lid from the west seam. It swings up about 100° on its east hinge, so the open well faces Jean and the lid's back faces her. The camera stays on her (east) side of the lid.
scenes.action_progression: Her speech (dialogue). He leans in (1.0) and puts his left hand on her right thigh (0.5). His speech, his eyes going to the tin twice. Her question; his line. The verdict: her left hand draws PR-30 out (1.0) and lays it flat (1.0); her right fingertip lifts (0.5); her right thumb raises the lid from the west seam toward her (1.0). Hold on his face (2.0). Cut.
scenes.emotional_shift: Before: fingertip on the lid, straw standing, face open and warm, hoping. Trigger: 'That's for you to find out', a line instead of a truth. After: her hands lay the straw flat and open the tin, while her face stays pleasant. The change is only in her hands.
scenes.transition_in: Hard cut in continuous time from SC12.
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut with an elision: from the open lid straight to SC14, with Jean already lifting her. What he takes from the tin, and how, stays off screen.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' PR-30 laid flat and PR-03 opening carry it: the hope of a picture with him alive goes down with the last straw, because he gave her a line. Cut this and the viewer loses why he dies, and that she wanted him to pass; SC18's photo would read as a trophy.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Tin interior. Acceptance: no frame ever shows into the well; the camera stays east of the raised lid. No contents, no preparation, no dosing (must avoid).
Wet mark on white gloss. Method: practical. Acceptance: it reads as a streak with no pooled liquid (lighting is the DP's).
Hand on thigh: practical, with an intimacy coordinator.

scenes.performance_beats: Jean's scene. Hero beat: close on his black-socked foot as it stops at the three drops, then steps over them. JEAN wants to get her to the bed; VENUS wants him to keep walking, and she never looks down. She turns his face back to hers with her right hand and says 'J.' It is the gesture she will repeat on him dead (V01-B07, SC18). Here, alive, he looks back.
scenes.blocking: From the sofa's north end JEAN stands and lifts VENUS from PR-44. He carries her past the table's north end, with the open tin and flat straw in view as they pass, then east across the rug to the hall and north to the bedroom door (x 540-630). PR-45 lies at x 575-600, y 880-886, just inside the threshold on the hall side. He stops with his lead foot short of the drops, then steps over into LOC-10.
scenes.action_progression: He stands (1.0) and lifts her (2.0). The carry, about 7 m (8.0). He looks down and stops for half a step (0.8). Her hand turns his face to hers (0.8); 'J.' (0.5). He steps over (1.0) and through the door (1.5).
scenes.emotional_shift: Jean's shift. Before: striding, eyes on her. Trigger: the drops at his feet. After: a half-step stop, eyes down. Second trigger: her hand on his jaw and 'J.' After: eyes up, he steps over and never looks back. Venus holds: she never looks down, because she doesn't know the drops are there.
scenes.transition_in: Hard cut with an elision from the open tin.
scenes.transition_out: Match cut: his black foot stepping over the drops on the white floor becomes his black shirt lying on the white floor just inside the bedroom door, later that night (SC15). The match is black on white at floor level.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' Her hand turning his face toward hers carries it: the last time he looks back. Cut this and the viewer loses the gesture's first, living use, so her turning his dead chin toward her (V01-B07) and toward the lens (SC18) has nothing to answer.
practical_or_compositing_flags: The carry. Method: practical, rehearsed with a stunt coordinator. Acceptance: steady, with no stumble.
Drops: 3-5 mm of dried crust that reads only in the close shot; no smear.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on her hand as it passes her phone on the nightstand and turns up the speaker ring over his catching breath. She wants to stop hearing his breathing. Tactic 1: she folds his black clothes square. Tactic 2: the mirror cabinet, with the same face and hands as the padlock check. She lifts the organiser, opens one lid, looks, closes it and puts it back, with no wince and no pause on the turned label: the meds are seen and never given as the reason. Real detail: she shuts the mirror door with her eyes down and never meets her reflection. Tactic 3: she lies down. His breathing stops, then catches with a rasp, and her hand passes the phone to reach the speaker. JEAN is breathing only, face down, recorded wild.
scenes.blocking: LOC-10: JEAN lies face down on the wall-D side of PR-52; VENUS is on the wall-B side. PR-56 is on the floor, the shirt at x 200, y 60 and the trousers at x 280, y 150; she folds them onto PR-55 (wall D). She goes out through the hall, passing the threshold drops without looking, to LOC-09: PR-50 on the middle shelf of PR-49, PR-51 on the top shelf with its label to the wall. Back in bed she lies on her back, head to wall C. PR-53 is on her right, with PR-01 face down (since SC11) 10 cm left of PR-54.
scenes.action_progression: She gathers the shirt (1.0) and the trousers (1.0), folds them (6.0) and sets them square on the chair, shirt on top (1.0). Walk to the bathroom (8.0). Opens the cabinet (0.8); lifts the organiser (1.0); opens row 1, column 1 (0.8); looks (1.5); closes it (0.5); puts it back (1.0); shuts the mirror door with her eyes down (0.8). Back to bed (8.0); lies down (2.0). His breathing runs slow and loud, stops for a gap (5.0), then rasps (1.0). Her right hand leaves the sheet (0.8), passes over the phone without slowing (0.5) and presses the speaker's dot, so the track plays low (0.5). She turns the ring to about 80% (2.0) and brings her hand back to her side (0.8). She lies still, eyes on the back of his head.
scenes.emotional_shift: Before: her hands stay busy with the folding and the cabinet. The organiser is a hold, with no trigger and no change, and the same face she gave the padlock. Trigger: his breath stops and catches with a rasp, which we hear. After: her hand goes past the phone to the music and turns it up until his breathing is under it. Then, for the first time, her hands go still.
scenes.transition_in: Match cut from SC14, black on white at floor level.
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut to morning with the track continuous: the same four bars loop across the cut, and the light on the same bed goes from night to morning.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' Her hand passing PR-01 for PR-54 carries it. The phone is her camera and the one thing that could call for help. Cut this and the viewer loses that she let him die while he could still be helped, so her waiting in SC16 and the photo in SC18 become love for a man she let go, not a collector's calm.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Meds. Acceptance: seen and never named; no legible label; all 28 compartments full. Risk: a close on the vial label or any diagnosis reads as the explanation (must avoid).
Breathing: wild sound, no lip-sync, face down.
Music: the original trance-soul track (A08), heard only from PR-54. Level changes come from her hand on the ring, not from the mix.
Mirror. Acceptance: no crew in the reflection, and she never meets her own. Speaker and phone back stay blank; no screen is ever lit or seen.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on his arm as she lifts it over her waist and it slides off. She wants him to turn over and reach for her. The look follows ref 06 as the brief describes it: he lies face down with his mouth open; she lies awake with a hand to her forehead, eyes on the back of his head, not the ceiling. This is the one scene where her hands have nothing to do. Tactic 1: she waits through another loop of the track. Tactic 2: the arm. Tactic 3: 'J. Stay for breakfast.', at the same dry pitch as 'That's a drink', not pleading. Then she switches the music off.
scenes.blocking: PR-52 is rumpled. JEAN lies face down on the wall-D side, his right arm off the bed on that side and his left arm toward her. VENUS is on the wall-B side. PR-54 is still looping at about 80%, with PR-01 face down beside it.
scenes.action_progression: Hold through a full loop (10.0); nothing moves but her breathing. She turns onto her side toward him (1.0), takes his left wrist (0.5) and lifts his arm over her waist (1.5). She lets go and it slides off onto the sheet (1.0). Her line (2.0). She waits (3.0). Her right hand goes to the speaker's dot and switches it off (1.0). Silence (hold 4.0).
scenes.emotional_shift: Before: still and waiting, a hand at her forehead. Triggers: his arm slides off her waist, which we see, and her line gets no answer, which we hear. After: she ends the music and the room goes silent. She stops waiting and gets up.
scenes.transition_in: The music bridges the cut from SC15.
scenes.transition_out: Hard cut on the silence to her hands at his shirt buttons (SC17).
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' His arm lifted over her waist carries it: she stages the picture of a couple waking up together, and it slides off. Cut this and the viewer loses the want at its plainest, feelings returned rather than sex (limerence), and the picture she can't make even here.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Jean's stillness. Method: practical breath-hold takes, or VFX paint-out of breathing. Acceptance: no rise in the chest across the take. Risk: one breath reads alive.
Arm slide. Method: practical, dead weight. Acceptance: it slides off rather than dropping stiffly.
Ref 06 is a look only, with no likeness; the bedding is white, not patterned, because the colour theme wins.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on the cloth as she scrubs out the three drops she missed until it is pink and the floor is white, then folds it square before she bins it. She wants the apartment spotless before she takes him away. She cleans with the same unhurried care she gave his collar, except at the threshold, the only place she speeds up. Real detail: the pink cloth folded into a 10 x 10 square before it goes in the bin. She puts her jacket back on before she touches the tin. The last image holds on the finished room longer than is comfortable: JEAN in black in the white armchair, sunglasses on, hands on the arms.
scenes.blocking: In LOC-10 she dresses him on the bed from the clothes folded on PR-55, and brings his shoes from PR-40. Cut: he is seated in PR-44 at the table's north end, facing south, hands on the arms, and she puts PR-04 on him with both hands. Back in the bedroom she takes PR-01 off PR-53 into her right front pocket, then strips and remakes PR-52. At the threshold (drops at x 575-600, y 880-886) she kneels on the bedroom side, facing south. The cloth goes into PR-60 (x 650-680, y 470-500). At the coffee table: the tumblers go to the kitchen run; her jacket comes off its hook (wall A, pending the production designer) and goes on; she closes PR-03 at x 140, y 525 from the east, behind its raised lid, and pockets it with PR-30 in her left jacket pocket; she wipes the table. She is out of frame for the final hold.
scenes.action_progression: Dressing: the shirt goes on (cut into the action), then the buttons (cut), about 20 s of screen time. Hard cut: he is seated in the armchair, the move itself elided. PR-04 on him (1.5). PR-01 off the nightstand into her pocket (1.0). She strips the bed (6.0), pulls the four fitted corners tight (8.0), and puts the duvet on and smooths it until only the ironed grid shows (6.0). Leaving the bedroom she looks down and stops (1.0), kneels (1.0) and scrubs, faster (6.0); the cloth is pink and the floor white (hold 1.0). She folds the cloth square (1.5), takes it to the bin, presses the pedal and drops it in as the lid soft-closes (4.0). Tumblers to the kitchen (3.0). Jacket off the hook and on (3.0). Her right hand pushes the raised lid shut from the east side (0.8); tin and straw into her left jacket pocket (1.5). She wipes the table, and the straw's wet mark goes with it (2.0). Hold on the room (10.0).
scenes.emotional_shift: Before: calm, methodical, never looking down. Trigger: the three drops at the threshold she had missed; it is the first time she looks down there. After: she kneels at once and scrubs harder and faster than at anything else, then folds the cloth square, back in control.
scenes.transition_out: Match cut from Jean seated in black in the white armchair, sunglasses on (SC17's hold), to Jean seated in black in PR-19 under his wall by lantern light, sunglasses off (SC18). The white room's silence becomes the wind at the motel door.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' Jean on PR-44 carries it: dressed, sunglasses on, posed at the centre of her spotless room, a portrait she makes of him and stays out of. Cut this and the viewer loses where the cold open's sunglasses and pose come from, and that she composes him for a picture rather than disposing of a body.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Closing the tin. Acceptance: the camera stays east of PR-03 and her hand closes the lid from behind it; no frame shows into the well (must avoid).
Dressing and moving a dead-weight actor: practical with a body double, elided with cuts, no struggle shown.
Pink cloth. Acceptance: pink (#E3A9A6), not red, with no drips. The scrubbed patch reads flatter and whiter than the satin floor.
Final hold: 8-10 s with nothing moving. Jean's stillness is tested as in SC16.
Car: nothing yet returns the two-seater from across the bar before SC01 (blocker with the writer).
Taste note broken on purpose, per the world bible: no dish rack and no charging cable, because the tidiness is the horror.

scenes.performance_beats: Venus's scene. Hero beat: close on her right thumb as it rests on the flip-camera icon and this time presses, and the screen shows both of them. She wants to get into one photograph with him. Her thumb rests as it did twice in the car. Then she lifts her head from his shoulder and looks round, past the back of his head, at the next man's two prints she has just pinned, and holds there: the wall has already moved on. She turns back, lays her head on his shoulder again and presses. For the first time her eyes go into a lens, her own front camera, and she is smiling. She turns his chin toward the lens; his gaze still passes under it. She takes the photo anyway with no disappointment played; the smile holds.
scenes.blocking: LOC-04, continuous from V01-B14. Jean was brought in off screen: he sits in PR-19 (x 210, y 420, facing south), face bare, eyes open. His head keeps the set from B07, 45° to his own right, so it points south-west, toward her side. VENUS unhooks PR-04, folds it and sets it lenses-up at x 135-149, y 365-370. From PR-06 under the window (wall A) she takes PR-28, pins already through them, and pins them in the paler rectangle on wall C at x 305-315, heights 170-185 and 188-203. She moves PR-18 to x 165 so its seat edge touches PR-19's. Both chairs face south, so she sits on his west side, his right, and rests her head on his right shoulder; her left hand is the one beside him. Her right hand holds PR-01 at arm's length in front of them to the south-west, front lens toward them, wall C behind. The phone is raised above his eye height, so his level, set gaze passes under the lens. The trigger look: she lifts her head and turns over her left shoulder, past the back of his head, to PR-28 at x 305-315, then back. Her left hand turns his chin toward the lens; rigor gives a few degrees sideways and can't lift it. She sets the phone face up beside PR-25, which ejects PR-27 to the south. She pins the card on wall C at x 290-295.4, heights 165-173.6, between Jean's photos and PR-28, and sits back down beside him.
scenes.action_progression: Sunglasses: unhook (1.0), fold (1.0), set down (0.8). To PR-06 (3.0); PR-28 out (2.0); to wall C (3.0); pins both (3.0). Moves PR-18 (1.5), sits (1.0), rests her head on his right shoulder (1.0). Her right hand takes PR-01 from her right front pocket (1.0) and raises it above his eye line (1.0). Thumb to the icon (0.8); it rests (1.2). She lifts her head and turns over her left shoulder to PR-28 (1.0); holds (1.0); turns back and lays her head on his shoulder again (1.0). She presses (0.3), and the screen shows both of them. Her left hand turns his chin (1.2); his eyes pass under the lens. Shutter (0.3). She sets the phone face up by the printer (1.0). The printer whirs and ejects the card (5.0). She takes the card from the slot (1.0), stands and pins it (3.0), then sits back down beside him (2.0). Key actions sum to 38.1 s; the rest of the 2:00 is the final hold.
scenes.emotional_shift: Before: her thumb rests on the icon (1.2 s), as it did twice in the car. Trigger, which the camera sees: she lifts her head from his shoulder and turns over her left shoulder, past the back of his head, to the next man's two prints on the wall, and holds there 1.0 s. After: she turns back, lays her head on his shoulder again and presses. The press is the change: her own face on her screen, eyes in the lens, smiling. Second beat, a hold: after her chin turn his gaze still passes under the lens, and she takes the picture with no change of face.
scenes.transition_in: Match cut from SC17: seated in black in the white chair becomes seated in black under the wall, with the wind at the door.
scenes.transition_out: End of the pilot. Hold on the wall (Jean's photos, the one card-size print of them together, the next man's two prints) with the two of them at the table below. Hard cut to black after the printer falls silent; the wind carries over the black.
scenes.campaign_idea_link: 'She isn't collecting trophies; she's trying to get into one photograph with him.' Her first press of the flip icon and PR-27 pinned between Jean's wall and the next man's carry it. Cut this and the viewer loses the answer to every thumb rest: she wanted one picture with him and gets it only when he can't look. They also lose the setup the series repeats.
practical_or_compositing_flags: Front-camera screen. Method: composite the UI. Acceptance: the lantern lights her face, her eyes are in the lens, and his gaze passes visibly under it.

Phone height. Acceptance: in the front-camera frame the lens sits above his eye line, so his eyes read level and below it, never into it. If a take shows his eyes meeting the lens, raise the phone; never re-pose his head (rigor).
Trigger look. Acceptance: her head leaves his shoulder, turns past the back of his head toward wall C, holds 1.0 s and returns before the press; it reads in the wide with the sound off.
PR-27. Method: a practical card pre-printed from the actual frame. Acceptance: with the sound off, it reads as the only card-size print on the wall.
Dead eyes: the same makeup lock as V01, no blink, lids at the top of the iris.
Contact with the dead man (head on his right shoulder, chin turn): practical, with a stillness-trained body double.
PR-28: a fictional man; the courthouse facade has no inscription or seal, and no real case is shown. The printer's whir is the only non-wind sound; no score.

assumptions: D01 scenes SC04-SC18 are staged for a live-action pilot shoot. Only V01, V02 and the stills are generated now, so the 5 s rule and the no-hand-off rule apply to those. The hand-offs in SC08 and SC12 (a phone and a glass) are practical only.

Venus holds the phone in her right hand throughout and drives with her left. This follows the world bible (PR-01 S2 and S6), S01 and her right-handedness, and it drives the hand staging in B02, B05, B07, B08 and SC18.
Wind is my choice. In the moving car it is relative, running nose to tail. At the motel it comes from the highway (south), which also explains the wind at room 3's south-facing door in B13.
B03's first jump (storefronts at 00:21:40, after the stop at 00:06:12) is staged as a second pass through the one block: she is circling the dead town.

Head set: after B07, Jean's face points north-east, 45° off the door toward the windscreen, held by rigor (casting). 'Head to the door' in B11 is read loosely as this set. Seated facing south in SC18, the same set points his face south-west, toward her side, which is why she holds the phone above his eye line.
SC13: Jean's near hand is his left, because the armchair (centre y 595) sits about 30 cm north of his seat at the sofa's north end (centre y 565).

The SC11 off-screen set (jacket off, tin onto the table, straw into her ice, phone to the nightstand) is done by Venus alone while Jean is in the bathroom; nothing passes between people, and it is heard only as ice.
SC07 is staged as written (LATER), with a hard cut and a time jump from SC06; the continuity question is filed with the writer, not assumed.
Phone and printer pair automatically in SC18, so there is no on-screen tapping to print.
The glovebox lid stays open after B09.
D01 timings cover the key physical actions; dialogue and holds fill the rest of each scene's slot.

There is no product, so claim_demo_needs_clearance doesn't arise. The verified story facts (the wall with none of them together, the gun in her back pocket at the motel, the meds untaken for weeks, the dried blood behind the toilet seat, the trance-soul music, Jean in black, the white colour theme) are staged exactly, with acceptance tests.

Taste notes broken on purpose: S01 shows her laughing face (a poster needs its lead); the B04 and B08 fallbacks show part of her face for under a second, as the route accepts; LOC-08 has no dish rack or charging cable because the tidiness is the horror. All others are followed: hands before faces, sound design before music, restraint over explanation, no slow motion.
No reference image was inspected. Refs 05 and 06 are used only as the brief describes them.
