blockers.issue: VENUS's hand anchors don't match the phone hand. The world bible (PR-01 S2 and S6) and S01 put the phone in her right hand, but casting puts the thumb nick on her left thumb for the flip-icon beats (V01-B04, B08, V02-B06, SC18) and the scar hand on the B02 collar. With the right-hand phone, her right thumb rests on the icon, her left hand touches the collar at the stop (B02), and her right hand turns his chin (B07).
blockers.resolution: Smallest fix: move the thumb nick to the right thumb and keep the right-hand scar, which then reads in B07 and on the phone hand. B02's left hand carries no anchor.

blockers.issue: PR-22, the two full water jugs, ride loose in the boot. On her one on-screen trip in B11 both shoulders and both arms are full, so the jugs can't reach the table in B12.
blockers.resolution: Pack both full jugs upright in grocery sack 2 under the oranges (they fit its 30 x 18 cm footprint) and update PR-07 and PR-22. B12 takes them out of sack 2, one per hand.

blockers.issue: PR-03 has no entry state for SC12. It is in her jacket pocket through SC10, and she enters SC12 in a pocketless T-shirt with a drink in each hand.
blockers.resolution: Pre-set it during SC11 (off screen, while she changes): closed on PR-42 at x 175, y 535, hinge east. PR-42's state at the head of SC12 becomes 'tin only'.

blockers.issue: Her jacket has no position from SC11, when she changes into the T-shirt, to SC17, when she puts it back on to pocket the tin and straw. It also has no V01 state. The SC11 off-screen set also moves PR-30 (jacket pocket to her tumbler's ice) and PR-01 (jacket pocket to PR-53) with no stated states.
blockers.resolution: Proposed: a single white hook on LOC-08 wall A beside the door, x 160, 170 cm up, out of the SC12-SC14 table frames. Add states: jacket on the hook SC11-SC17; PR-30 in her tumbler from SC11; PR-01 on PR-53 from SC11. From SC17 the stylist decides whether she wears the jacket (with PR-03 and PR-30) in V01 or it travels in PR-06.

blockers.issue: Jean's sunglasses (PR-04) first appear on him in SC17, with no earlier state or source.
blockers.resolution: Hook them in the placket of his black shirt from SC04 (a night-time affectation that suits his swagger). They ride on top of the folded shirt in SC15, and she takes them from there in SC17.

blockers.issue: PR-01 has no state between SC04 and SC15, or between V01-B08 and SC18, and she needs both hands in B09-B12.
blockers.resolution: Right jacket pocket SC04-SC10. Face down on PR-53 from SC11 (the off-screen set) until SC17, when she pockets it. In her right hand through V01-B01 to B08. Right front jeans pocket from B09 (set across the cut) until SC18. The stylist confirms a front pocket that holds 15 x 7.2 cm.

blockers.issue: V01-B05 switches on the video light, but the picture is her screen, so an on-screen control would show; PR-01 as described has no physical button.
blockers.resolution: Add one plain, unmarked side button to PR-01's frame edge, under her right index finger when she holds it upright. The press happens off picture and the UI never changes.

blockers.issue: In LOC-02 the storefronts sit south of the crossroads, yet B03's first jump shows storefronts about 15 minutes after the 00:06:12 stop at that crossroads.
blockers.resolution: Confirm a loop route (east on the gravel road and back to the town's south end) so B03's storefront cut is a second northbound pass through the same block. No new build is needed.

blockers.issue: SC18 has no source for the three pins: two for PR-28 and one for PR-27.
blockers.resolution: The next man's prints come out of PR-06 with pins already through their top edges, plus one spare pin in the top print for PR-27.

blockers.issue: V02-B04 to B06 need about 7 s of phone-frame footage on Jean's open eyes, but V01-B08's phone section runs only 3.6 s.
blockers.resolution: Generate the B08 eyes plate with handles (two plates of up to 5 s joined on a laugh jolt) at 1080x1920 or better, and shoot the thumb composite plate long.

blockers.issue: SC06 ends on Venus's 'My turn' and SC07 opens with Jean taking her turn, which plays as continuous, but SC07's heading says LATER. Staged as written: a hard cut with a time jump and lower coupes.
blockers.resolution: Smallest fix: change SC07's heading to CONTINUOUS, which lets SC06 cut on action into his hand sliding the candle. Otherwise keep LATER and leave the staging as it is.

blockers.issue: Her two-seater is left parked across from the bar in SC08 (they leave by rideshare), and she has it for the drive in SC01. No scene gets it back.
blockers.resolution: Smallest fix: add one line to SC17, before she dresses Jean: a 4 s insert of the two-seater, top down, pulled up at her building's kerb in daylight. No dialogue.

blockers.issue: SC11 carries plot (A13, the previous man's drops) but has no honest link to the route idea; nothing on screen ties the drops to a photograph. Staged as written, and the link field says so.
blockers.resolution: Writer's call: accept SC11 as a plot scene while SC18 carries the idea. Or add a 2 s beat before he lifts the seat, where Jean takes a mirror selfie in PR-49 (PR-35): him alone in her home, one more photo with no her in it.

evidence.specificity: The cinematographer and storyboard artist could board almost every beat from the page without calling anyone. Each beat has marks from the world bible, timings that add up, and the props and each hand tracked. Example: "B02, 4.0-10.0: the car rolls to a full stop and the frame dips (0.8); her left hand leaves the wheel and enters under the lens (0.7); two strokes brush the shoulder and collar points back to black, C1 to C2 (1.2); she pinches the left collar point flat (1.0); her hand rests on the collar (0.8); hidden cut at 8.9 as the withdrawing hand wipes the lens (0.4); the frame lurches as she pulls away over PR-58 (1.1)." The physical state added since the last round is just as exact: "PR-03 closed onto PR-42 at x 175, y 535; PR-01 from her right jacket pocket face down on PR-53 in the bedroom." Two places would still prompt a question. In SC08, "frames him and shoots (1.3)" doesn't say which camera is on, or which way his phone faces. In SC18, "Key actions sum to 38.1 s; the rest of the 2:00 is the final hold" leaves about 80 s that nothing fills.
evidence.distinctiveness: This direction could only belong to LIMERENCE. The rest-and-slide gesture runs through the whole pilot: her thumb on the flip icon (2.2 s, then 1.2 s), her fingertip on the chimney straw, her fingertip on the tin, and finally the press. The details are ones nobody else would have written: "Real detail: she obeys the stop line on an empty road and still finishes dressing him." and "Her right hand leaves the sheet (0.8), passes over the phone without slowing (0.5) and presses the speaker's dot, so the track plays low (0.5)." The payoff is also specific to this story: "She takes the photo anyway with no disappointment played; the smile holds."
evidence.fit: Every must-include is staged, and every must-avoid is written as a test someone can check. Examples: "Meds. Acceptance: seen and never named; no legible label; all 28 compartments full." and "Tin interior. Acceptance: no frame ever shows into the well; the camera stays east of the raised lid." The route idea is now tied to something the camera sees in every link. Example: "PR-01 carries it: its bare black edge shows at her right jacket pocket through the whole scene, and her right hand goes to the straws and to his forearm, never to it." Approved material is no longer rewritten. SC07's LATER, the car that is never retrieved and SC11's weak idea link all go to the writer as blockers with the smallest fix. The taste notes it breaks are named and justified.
evidence.craft:
All six previous notes are fixed.
- SC18: she now rests her head on his right shoulder, and the trigger is a head turn the camera sees: "Thumb to the icon (0.8); it rests (1.2). She lifts her head and turns over her left shoulder to PR-28 (1.0); holds (1.0); turns back and lays her head on his shoulder again (1.0). She presses (0.3), and the screen shows both of them." The scene's timings add up to 38.1 s, as stated.
- B07: the camera axis is restated in world terms ("From 45.0 the B07 axis sits ahead of the windscreen, on or just west of the centreline").
- B05: the light is switched by a named side button.
- SC03: the chair now gets 3.3 s against 1.8 s for the cans.
- SC11: an off-screen reset is stated. SC12 sets the tin's hinge to the east, and SC13's hands are correct.
- The transitions from SC03 into SC04 are now called hard cuts.
- The flame flag for SC07 is in.
What stops it short of 9:
- V01-B09 says "lifts PR-02 out by the grip, muzzle down (0.7)" from a glovebox at Jean's knees, which breaks its own test ("the muzzle never crosses Jean").
- SC18's "Hard cut to black after the printer falls silent" contradicts "the rest of the 2:00 is the final hold".
- In SC07, a man on stool 2 (y 350) "reaches across her to the caddy (x 130, y 480)", about 1.4 m away, without getting up.

notes.target: SC18 action_progression and transition_out; running time of SC11, SC14, SC16 and SC18
notes.note:
SC18 contradicts itself. "Key actions sum to 38.1 s; the rest of the 2:00 is the final hold" means about 80 s of static frame. Meanwhile "Hard cut to black after the printer falls silent" would cut at about 32 s, before she has pinned PR-27.

Fix SC18: after she sits back down (38.1), hold the wide of the two of them under the wall for a stated length, e.g. 8-10 s to match SC17's hold, with nothing moving but the wind at the door. Then hard cut to black with the wind carrying over. Rewrite transition_out so the cut comes after she sits, not after the printer.

The same gap runs through the other scenes with little or no dialogue. As staged: SC11 is about 13 s of a 60 s slot, SC14 about 16 s of 90, SC16 about 24 s of 90, SC18 about 48 s of 120. Check SC15 (about 44 of 150) and SC17 (about 77 of 150) as well. That is several minutes of the ~30-minute outline that no staging fills, and "dialogue and holds fill the rest" can't cover scenes with no dialogue.

Write each scene's staged running time next to its slot. Then file one blocker with the writer, with the smallest fix: re-time those slots and move the spare minutes to the bar or the apartment dialogue, or accept a shorter episode. Don't pad the scenes with holds.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Time actions as sub-steps in seconds. They sum to the script beat, or you name where the cut goes into the action'; 'If a scene fails the test or can't be staged in its time, stage it as written and file a blocker with the smallest fix'; 'Every transition is motivated'

notes.target: V01-B09 (SC02) and SC04: pistol handling
notes.note:
In B09, "lifts PR-02 out by the grip, muzzle down (0.7)" from the passenger glovebox points the muzzle into Jean's footwell, at his knees. That breaks your own acceptance test ("the muzzle never crosses Jean or the lens"). Jean is also played by a living actor.

Restage it so the muzzle points toward the dash, north, from the glovebox all the way to her back pocket. Rewrite the performance line "keeping the muzzle down and away from him" to match. Apply the same rule in SC04, where she draws the pistol from her back pocket while seated and lays it in the glovebox.

In both flags, name the method for every practical plate: a non-firing replica handled under an armourer or the props master. Mark it pending with the producer.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Flag what a crew or a model will get wrong... Each flag gives a method... an acceptance test... and the risk'; quality bar Craft: 'nothing physically implausible'; 'Every right and consent the work needs is named with its source, scope and owner and left pending for the producer'

notes.target: SC08 last call: Jean's front camera (PR-35) and Venus's eyes
notes.note:
At the scene's hero beat, the camera and screen state is unstated. "She takes it (0.8), leans back out of frame (0.6), frames him and shoots (1.3)" could be read as her flipping his camera, and it never says where her eyes go while his front camera has both of them in frame.

State both:
(a) While Jean holds PR-35 out, the front camera frames both of them for about 1.0 s. Her eyes stay on him, never on his lens. The casting lock says her first look into any lens is SC18, and you already hold this rule in SC09.
(b) She takes the phone and keeps it where his arm held it: front camera still on, screen toward Jean. She leans back out of its frame and presses only the shutter, never a flip icon, so SC18's press is still the first flip of the camera toward herself.

Add an acceptance test to the phone flag: her eyes are never on PR-35's lens, and no camera-flip control is touched.
notes.source: Route R2: 'the front camera turns on only once per man, at the table, afterwards'; casting bible VENUS lens rule ('her eyes never go into any lens... The first time is SC18'); craft brief 'Physical state is tracked, beat by beat'

notes.target: SC06 to SC08: position of stool 3 after the slide, and Jean's reach in SC07
notes.note:
In SC06, "she slides her stool toward his until the gap between the seats is gone", but SC07 and SC08 never say where stool 3 sits afterwards. Several marks were set from stool 3 at y 440: the straw house (centred y 395), her coupe (y 440), the candle "on her side" (y 418) and S03's "between two glasses". If she stays at about y 395, the house sits in front of her rather than between them.

State whether she stays close or slides back across the LATER cut, and re-check those marks.

Separately, in SC07 "He reaches across her to the caddy (x 130, y 480)" asks a seated man on stool 2 (y 350) to reach about 1.4 m. Stage it as a big move: he rises off his stool and leans across her, with the sub-step timed (about 1.5 s instead of 1.0). That also keeps his arm crossing in front of her, which the scene wants.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Each beat starts from the state the last left: position...'; 'Blocking is geography'; quality bar Craft: 'nothing physically implausible'

notes.target: SC02/SC03 transition and the SC13 lid (wording fixes)
notes.note:
(a) SC02's transition_out says the cut lands "where the lantern click lights the wall". But SC03 plate A has the sacks set down first (0.8) and the click after (0.6). Either put the click first (click 0.6, then sacks 0.8, same 5.0 s), or make the transition say the first 0.8 s of SC03 is black with the sacks landing on the table heard only as sound.
(b) In SC13, "her right thumb raises the lid from the west seam toward her" and "the lid's back faces her" don't fit an east hinge with her sitting north of the tin. Lifted from the west seam, the lid swings up and back to the east, so its back faces the camera on the east side. Say that, so the rule that no frame shows the well is described correctly.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Every transition is motivated... what carries across and where the eye sits on each side'; 'Blocking is geography'

keep: The rest-and-slide gesture chain: thumb on the flip icon in B04 (2.2 s, shyness) and B08 (1.2 s, 'not like this, not yet'); fingertip on the chimney straw (SC07); fingertip holding the tin shut (SC12), then lifting after his line (SC13); the first press in SC18
SC18's visible trigger (head lifts off his shoulder, turns over her left shoulder to PR-28, holds 1.0 s, returns), then the press, with her head on his right shoulder and the 38.1 s sum

The B07 axis fix: west side up to 45.0, then a cut on action to an axis ahead of the windscreen; his face set north-east, gaze passing the lens on its east side; V02-B03's hand and face kept in the middle third
The SC18 phone held above his eye line so his set gaze passes under it, with the rule 'raise the phone; never re-pose his head'
SC15: her hand passes PR-01 without slowing to turn up the speaker ring over the rasp; the meds played with the same face and hands as the padlock check
SC03's rebalanced plates (chair 3.3 s against 1.8 s for the cans) and the head turn to the bare boards as trigger

The SC11 off-screen reset (jacket on the hook, tin to PR-42, straw into her ice, phone to PR-53), SC12's tin set hinge east with the seam toward Jean, and the jacket back on before the tin closes in SC17
SC05's campaign link anchored on PR-01's bare edge in her pocket, never touched; SC10's 0.8 s step back to her filming distance
The honest SC11 link and its writer blocker; the SC07 LATER and car-return blockers with their smallest fixes
Tin interior never framed: the camera stays east of the raised lid in SC13 and SC17
Blockers with their fixes: jugs packed in sack 2, the PR-01 side button, the thumb nick moved to the right thumb, the sunglasses' source, pins for SC18
No generated lip-sync anywhere; phone and glass hand-offs practical only; no slow motion; taste-note breaks declared (S01 face, no dish rack in LOC-08)

assumptions: Season and temperature are assumed: early October 2026 in the US Southwest (the world bible gives only 'US, 2026 ASSUMED'). That puts the city at night at about 19 °C, the apartment at 21 °C, the desert drive at 27 °C falling to 17 °C, and the motel at night at about 15 °C.

US sizing follows the casting bible's assumption. Skin depth and undertone are read from the casting bible's cheekbone hexes. Heritage is recorded there and never prompted, so every look restates depth, undertone and curl pattern instead.

Jean's black: the route and set palettes use #111111, which I treat as the graded read. The fabric in a neutral grade is blue-black #24262B (approx L*15), per the craft rule that blacks sit near L* 15-22.

Note 1 is applied, with one number corrected. At the high hip, 2 cm above the back pockets, only 2 cm of the 6 cm grip would clear the hem; the other 4 cm would sit under the back of the jacket. I cut the hem 7 cm above the pocket tops instead (at the waist, 1 cm above the waistband), so PR-02 S1 holds exactly as written. To still end above that hem, the inside left pocket moves up: welt 2 cm above the armhole base, bag 22 cm (not 24). That still takes the 20 cm straw. A waist-length jacket never reaches her lap, so no sit fold forms at all. The wide lock reads 'at the waist' rather than 'at the high hip' for this reason. The old blocker 2 is withdrawn.

Note 2: the sleeve landmark is locked at the roll's lower edge, 12 cm above the wrist bone. Two 6 cm turns on a sleeve that ends at the wrist bone put the top of the roll at 18 cm, so the lower edge is what matches the L01 cuff edge. The seated creases sit just above the belt, not below it, because below the belt the shirt is tucked out of sight. The 'second hole' claim is cut: her belt stays on its middle hole in every look.

Note 3: Jean's builds (SH-1 to SH-4, TR-1, TR-2, belt x2, Derbies x2) are mapped to scenes and beats. SH-4's split never appears in V01 0-56 s, because the phone films the back of his collar there. The belt is on hole 1, nearest the buckle (the loosest), 5 cm out from the old middle-hole crease.
Note 5: L02's fastened top button is carried by the 44 cm collar band on SH-2 to SH-4. The band size never shows in L01, where the top button is open.

Note 6 is answered both ways. Raglan oatmeal sleeves and a V-notch rib give the tee an athletic read in a wide, and oatmeal stays within the white room (C*10, L*81). I also state plainly that the team itself (Lucas's Raptors) is lost until A10 clears it or a fictional team is designed; this is flagged to Lucas.

Venus changes looks only when the story does: the bar (L01), the tee at home (L02, changed off screen in SC11), then the shirt for the drive (L03, from SC17). The bone jacket comes back at the end of SC17 to take the tin and flat straw, then goes folded into the boot, unseen, through V01.
The nape puff for the open car is the stylist's call, per the casting bible. It keeps hair off the hand shots and avoids the slow-motion hair the brief bans.

There is no product (R2 stretch), so the product hue rule was run against the story's two reds instead: the REC dot #D7261E and the dried drops #6E1C18. Every garment worn in frame with them is under C* 15 or far off in hue. Skin and hair are excluded: skin is never altered, and hair belongs to the casting anchors.

Every look has one garment older than the story, with a rebuild method: Venus's pistol-worn back pocket and her L02 tee, Jean's belt, the bartender's apron, and the driver's sun-faded shirt (taste note: one real detail per scene).

Taste notes followed: hands before faces (every acting hand is bare, with cuffs at mid-forearm or above) and restraint over explanation (no signature jewellery or symbolic pieces; her whites and his black carry the verified colour theme). One craft rule is broken on purpose: VENUS_L02 sits inside the white room's palette so that Jean is the only dark mass, because the tone makes the room's tidiness the horror.
No reference image was inspected, since no reference_reader is bound. Refs 02 and 06 are used only as the brief describes them, and no character is modelled on a face in them.

blockers.issue: The hands conflict between departments. PR-01 puts the phone in Venus's right hand while she records (V01-B01 to B05, B08), which makes her left hand the free one that brushes his collar in B02. The casting bible anchors the collar and chin touches on her right-hand scar, and the flip-icon thumb on her left-thumb nick.
blockers.responsible_agent: Storyboard artist with casting director and production designer
blockers.resolution: Wardrobe works either way: both sleeves end 12 cm above the wrist bone and both hands are bare in VENUS_L01 and L03. Storyboard picks the hand for each beat, and casting moves the anchors to match (for example, the nick on the right thumb if the right hand holds the phone).

blockers.issue: Jean's black is #111111 in the route and set palettes (PR-04, PR-56, the LOC-01 contrast note of 11.8:1). The costume is specified as blue-black #24262B fabric, per the craft rule for blacks at L* 15-22. PR-41 is confirmed at #2A2624, not #151515.
blockers.resolution: The colourist grades Jean toward the route's #111111 read; ungraded, the fabric still gives 9.5:1 on the bone headrest #D9CBB0. Production design updates the PR-41 and PR-56 hexes and notes the SH-1 to SH-4 and TR-1/TR-2 builds against PR-56's states.

blockers.issue: Lucas's 'oversized Raptors t shirt' loses its team. The L02 tee reads as an athletic shirt by its raglan cut and V-notch, but no team, city or colour can be shown until A10 clears the real shirt or a fictional team is designed and cleared.
blockers.responsible_agent: Lucas (creative lead) via producer, with production designer
blockers.resolution: Lucas chooses: accept the unmarked athletic tee, or have production design create a fictional team for the producer to clear under A10. If team colours come in, wardrobe re-runs the white-room rule break, because a saturated or dark team colour would make a second mass beside Jean.

blockers.issue: Heritage for VENUS and JEAN is still for Lucas to confirm (carried over from the casting bible). Hair and makeup here are written in skin depth, undertone and curl pattern only.
blockers.resolution: If casting changes, only the skin hexes, curl patterns and grooming lines in VENUS_L01-L03 and JEAN_L01-L02 need updating. The garments stand.

evidence.specificity: All six notes from the last review are addressed. On two of them the revision also corrected the reviewer's suggested numbers. Garments are placed by landmark and measurement, so someone could rebuild them from the rail on day three without asking. For example: "Inside left pocket: welt 14 cm wide, 2 cm above the armhole base. Bag 22 cm deep, ending 2 cm above the hem; her armhole base sits 22 cm above the hem line." The sleeve now has one landmark: "Two 6 cm turns put the roll's lower edge 12 cm above the wrist bone, the same landmark as the L01 cuff." Crease states are numbered ("S2, from V01-B01: two horizontal creases across the front just above the belt ... and one diagonal crease in each inner elbow"). Jean's builds are tied to beats ("SH-3, dust repeat ... swapped in for each retake of V01-B02 and V02-B01"). The stated values check out: #24262B is L*15, #F2EEE6 is L*94 and #8FA3B8 is L*66, and the 9.5:1 and 5.5:1 contrast ratios are correct. It stays at 9, not 10, because one insert lock has the belt direction backwards (see craft).
evidence.distinctiveness: The key details only make sense for this story. "Older than the story: the right back pocket is faded to #A9B9C9 in a 12 x 9 cm outline of the pistol, and its top edge is frayed." "The fastened top button is the change the camera sees: it sits at the collar her hand straightens in V01-B02, and he'd never have done it himself." "A flat chain weight in the hem facing of both fronts, so they hang the same with or without PR-03." The anchor on the left side of Jean's neck also serves as a check against generator mirroring: "A mole on the right means the frame is mirrored: reject it." The onlookers have their own lives too: the driver's "left shoulder and left sleeve are sun-faded to #97A28E from the driver's window." The L02 tee is still the plainest look. It is now earned by "Raglan oatmeal sleeves and a V-notch rib", and the loss of Lucas's team shirt is flagged openly instead of glossed over.
evidence.fit: The verified colour facts drive the looks rather than decorate them: "Rule broken on purpose ... so she belongs to the white room, her skin and dark curls carry her read, and JEAN stays the only dark mass (verified: 'The colour theme is white'; tone: clean)." Jean's black follows the verified fact and is reconciled with the route's #111111 as a graded read. The must-avoids hold. Nudity: "Lucas's 'no underwear' is implied, never shown", and the SC14 carry is capped at "no higher than 15 cm above the knee". Brands: "No logo, lettering or trade dress on any piece", including denim pocket stitching and sole colour. Faces: "No reference image was inspected ... no character is modelled on a face in them." The route's clear zone is carried into wardrobe: "no cuff, hair or strap enters the lower-right 15% of the phone frame; only her thumb does." Lucas's Raptors shirt is correctly sent back to him as blocker 3 instead of being claimed as kept. Hair and makeup restate depth, undertone and curl pattern in every look, with "Do not lighten the skin, de-age her or smooth the texture."
evidence.craft: This is senior technique, and in places it corrects the reviewer. "At the high hip, 2 cm above the back pockets, only 2 cm of the 6 cm grip would clear the hem ... I cut the hem 7 cm above the pocket tops instead." "Two 6 cm turns on a sleeve that ends at the wrist bone put the top of the roll at 18 cm, so the lower edge is what matches the L01 cuff edge." The dead-weight builds are practical and complete: "SH-4, dressing double: ... a centre-back split from the collar band to the hem, closed by 7 flat snaps"; "TR-2 ... invisible zip in the right side seam"; "a pair half a size up with the laces pre-set loose." What holds it at 8: one locked detail is physically backwards, and it comes from the last review's own wording. "Brown-black belt on hole 1, the hole nearest the buckle (the loosest)" is wrong, because the hole nearest the buckle end is the tightest. As locked ("the cracked crease at the middle hole sits 5 cm past the buckle"), the belt tells the story of a man who lost weight. There are also two small continuity gaps. The L03 shirt is locked "pressed, no creases" through all of SC17's physical work. The jacket is "folded in the boot, never seen" in a scene (V01-B11) where she opens the boot. Every fix is a single line.

Name the swap point inside SC17: SH-4 while her hands are on him, SH-2 from the held wide frame in PR-44. The chest fold crease is pressed identically into both. The duplicate plan then reads as a single order of use.
notes.source: Craft brief: a look is finished when someone could pull it from a rail and rebuild it on day three without asking; changes inside a scene are locked states, with the beat where they start

notes.source: Quality bar, what always costs points: banned language ('seamless')

cues.description: Inside the phone. From frame 1, open-car wind hits a single phone mic, and the phone's limiter pumps and clips on every gust. Under it are the small engine at cruise and the tyres slapping road seams as the empty town goes by. Off screen, one loose shop awning flaps as they pass (2.2 s, f53). Absent: traffic, voices, dogs and any car stereo, because the town is empty. Her laugh sits on top from 0.5 s (SND-V01-015).
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production. Wind and engine are captured on a phone mic held at arm's length in a hired vintage open two-seater at road speed, on an empty road, with no third-party voices. Scope: all media, worldwide, in perpetuity from first use, for V01, V02, the pitch-deck embed and the pilot; owned by the production. The vehicle-hire and location agreements must allow recording and use, and no make is to be identified. Status: required, pending. Next step and owner: the producer books the car and the recordist.

cues.description: Hard cut at 4.0 (f96) onto the car already braking. The wind is at half and gone by 4.8 (f115), when the car settles on its springs with a small creak. The engine idles, a little lumpy, from 4.8 to 8.8. Far off, a tin sign creaks once on its chain (5.2, f125): the only other sound in town. Her fingertips brush dust off his black cotton shirt, close on the mic, in three strokes at 5.6, 6.1 and 6.6 s (f134, f146, f158). The collar is pressed flat at 7.6 (f182). Jean makes no sound. The clutch takes up and the engine pulls away at 8.8 (f211), and the wind is back on the mic at 9.4 (f226). All picture-led, ±2 frames. V02-B01 cuts in at 6.5 s (SND-V02-001). Fallback, where her hand only rests on his collar: drop the strokes and keep one fabric touch at 5.8 (f139).
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production (cotton shirt, fingertips), with the idle and pull-away from the SND-V01-001 car session; scope as SND-V01-001. The sign creak is recorded on location, or taken from a library under a non-exclusive licence: all media, worldwide, term from first use in perpetuity (or the term the producer sets), covering V01, V02, the pitch-deck embed and the pilot. Status: required, pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: The wind roar cuts hard three times, on the picture's three jump cuts. Picture-led: each audio cut sits on the same frame as its picture cut. Each roar belongs to a different place. At 10.0 (REC 00:21:40) it is the town, bouncing off storefronts. At 12.5 (REC 00:38:15) it is open desert, broad and even. At 15.0 (REC 00:52:30) it is the scrub hills, gusty, with the limiter clamping hard. Each cut lands on a fresh snatch of her laugh (SND-V01-015). 15.0-18.0 s, the scrub hills, is the loudest point in V01. V02-B02 cuts in at 15.0 (SND-V02-002). No whoosh or riser on any cut: the roar itself is the cut.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production in the SND-V01-001 phone-mic car session. Scope as SND-V01-001. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Wind on the mic, a little less roar now that the sun is lower. Her thumb on the glass is loud because the mic is right beside it. It squeaks across the screen to the flip icon from 19.4 to 20.0 (f466-f480), makes a small pressure knock in the phone body as it rests at 20.0 (f480), then slides away from 22.4 to 22.9 (f538-f550). The icon itself makes no tick or UI sound. Her laugh, shorter, at 23.3 (f559). Picture-led, ±2 frames. These thumb takes come back in SND-V02-006 and in the tag (SND-D01-003). Fallback (the under-a-second front-camera flip): a 2-frame audio dropout at the flip and again at the flip back, and no camera sound.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production on a debadged phone. No manufacturer UI sound is used anywhere; the phone UI is an original design, with clearance pending with the producer under A10. Scope as SND-V01-001; owned by the production. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Hard cut at 26.0 (f624) to blue dusk. The wind on the mic eases as the car slows, and tyres on grit come up underneath. A fingertip taps the glass at 27.0 (f648), and the video light comes on at f650, so the tap leads the light by two frames (picture-led, ±2). The light and the glint on his collar get no sound: no hum, drone or sting. No laugh in this beat.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production (car session and phone foley). Scope as SND-V01-001. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: 34.0-34.4 (f816-f826): a handling rumble on the phone mic as she lowers the phone. At 34.4 (f826) the frame opens to full width, the phone mic cuts, and we hear the world from outside the car. The wind drops away. The two-seater's engine and tyres on grit are heard from a locked-off position at the roadside, with a light breeze in dry creosote. Absent: birds, insects and any other engine. This is the first clean, quiet sound in V01. Her laugh, further off, at 36.0 (SND-V01-015). Picture-led, ±2 frames: the switch lands on the frame where the picture widens.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: exterior car passes recorded for this production (SND-V01-001 session; scope as there). The desert dusk atmos is recorded on location, or taken from a library under a non-exclusive licence: all media, worldwide, term from first use in perpetuity (or the term the producer sets), covering V01, V02, the pitch-deck embed and the pilot. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Closer perspective; the engine and tyres drop low. The arm of the sunglasses slides out of his hair with a dry scratch at 43.0 (f1032). Two fingers on his chin: his cheek leaves the leather headrest with a short creak at 44.6 (f1070), and his collar shifts. From 45.5 (f1092) to 50.0 we hold on the eyes. The only sound near him is his black cotton collar fluttering against his neck in the wind, soft and close, over the low engine. No laugh, no breath from him, and no sting or drone. This is the quietest moment of the drive: the missing laugh is the reveal. Picture-led, ±2 frames. V02-B03 cuts in at 42.8 s (SND-V02-003). Fallback A16 (car parked at the motel): same foley with the engine off, and cooling-engine ticks from SND-V01-009 in place of the tyres.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production (acetate sunglasses, leather headrest, cotton collar). Scope as SND-V01-001; owned by the production. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.timing: V01-B08, 50.0-56.0 s; switch back to the phone mic at 51.6 s (f1238)
cues.description: An acetate hinge ticks as she hooks one open arm of the sunglasses into her neckline (50.5, f1212). She raises the phone from 51.0 to 51.6 with a handling rumble. At 51.6 (f1238) the frame narrows to upright and the sound cuts back to the phone mic: the wind returns, lower than in daylight. Her laugh, softer and close, at 52.4 (SND-V01-015). Her thumb squeaks onto the flip icon from 53.8 to 54.2 (f1291-f1301), rests, and slides back from 55.0 to 55.4 (f1320-f1330). Hard out at 56.0 (f1344), on the cut. Picture-led, ±2 frames. V02-B04 to B06 need a longer phone-frame take than this 4.4 s (flag in SND-V02-004 and blockers). Fallback: 2-frame dropouts at the flip and the flip back, as in SND-V01-004.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production, with the wind from the SND-V01-001 session. Scope as SND-V01-001; owned by the production. No manufacturer UI sound (A10). Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Hard cut at 56.0 to the motel carport, engine off. The cooling exhaust pings irregularly, the first ping at 56.3 (f1351). Dry palm fronds rattle in the wind, and the carport's sheet roof ticks. The glovebox push-button latch releases and the lid drops onto its stays at 57.4 (f1378). The pistol's steel knocks the glovebox floor once as she lifts it (58.0, f1392), and it slides into her denim back pocket at 59.0 (f1416). No slide rack, no hammer click and no metal sting: the gun is carried, not introduced. Picture-led, ±2 frames. Fallback (pistol already in her pocket): drop the latch, the knock and the slide.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: gun-handling foley recorded for this production with a non-firing replica under the production's prop-safety protocol; the latch and engine ticks from the car session; owned by the production, scope as SND-V01-001. The palms and carport roof are recorded on location, or taken from a library under a non-exclusive licence: all media, worldwide, term from first use in perpetuity (or the term the producer sets), covering V01, V02, the pitch-deck embed and the pilot. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Her boots on gravel along the frontage from 60.0, a step roughly every 0.55 s. The loose steel panel on the MOTEL sign ticks in the wind, out of step with her feet. She tugs the padlock and the shackle knocks the hasp twice, at 62.2 and 62.5 (f1493, f1500). Her steps stop at 62.8 (f1507). From 62.8 to 64.0 there is only wind and the sign ticking while she looks at the unbroken dust. Picture-led, ±2 frames.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production (boots, gravel, padlock); scope as SND-V01-001. The sign tick is recorded on location, or taken from a library under a non-exclusive licence: all media, worldwide, term from first use in perpetuity (or the term the producer sets), covering V01, V02, the pitch-deck embed and the pilot. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: The boot-lid latch at 64.4 (f1546), then its hinge. His black nylon bag is dragged out from 65.2 to 65.8, then her bag. Two paper grocery sacks crackle, with cans shifting inside, from 66.5 to 68.0. Gravel steps to the room from 68.0 to 69.8. Her shoulder thumps the swollen door at 70.2 (f1685), and it scrapes open over grit from 70.3 to 71.6. The palms and the sign tick from SND-V01-009 and 010 continue underneath. Jean makes no sound. Picture-led, ±2 frames.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production, with the boot lid from the car session. Scope as SND-V01-001; owned by the production. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Hard cut inside. The room tone is a sealed, dead room, with the wind muffled through the door and the roof ticking as it cools. Absent: any hum, fridge or buzz, because there is no power here. The lantern's plastic switch clicks at 72.4 (f1738), two frames before the light comes up (f1740). Her hands then set things down: cans on wood at 74.0, 74.6 and 75.2 (f1776, f1790, f1805); a full water jug with the water slapping inside at 76.2 (f1829); two oranges, soft thuds, at 77.2 and 77.6 (f1853, f1862); the hollow plastic of the photo printer at 78.8 (f1891). A chair leg drags across the boards from 80.0 to 81.2 (f1920-f1949). Nothing sounds after 81.2. Picture-led, ±2 frames.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production, with room tone recorded in a real derelict room or an empty timber room (location release required). The printer is recorded on a debadged unit. Scope as SND-V01-001; owned by the production. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Held frame. Nothing in the room moves, so nothing in the room is heard. Only the wind outside, pushing at the swollen door: its latch knocks in the keeper twice, at 83.6 and 86.2 (f2006, f2069), and the last gust dies away by 87.8 (f2107). Room tone continues underneath. Sound-led: the picture stays still and nothing needs to hit these knocks.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production in the SND-V01-012 room session (wind and door latch). Scope as SND-V01-012. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: At 88.0 (f2112), on the frame where the LIMERENCE card lands, all sound cuts hard, room tone included. Digital silence runs to 90.0. No sting and no title hit. Sound-led, ±2 frames: the card and the cut share the frame. This is the quietest point in V01: the title lands on a room with nobody in it.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: None required, because no audio is used. At conform, check that no room tone or reverb tail runs past f2112. The title card is the only brand asset, and the piece is unbranded.

cues.description: The laugh is Venus's only voice in V01 (A15). Jean makes no sound anywhere, not even breath. B01: loud and right on the mic, landing on the picture's jolt (picture-led, ±2). B03: a different snatch on each cut. B04: shorter. B06: further off. B08: softer and close. No laugh in B07. Read: aimed at him, as if he is in on the joke; delight, not mania. It must never sound like a villain's laugh or a horror cue. B01, B03, B04 and B08 are off-mouth, because she is behind the phone. B06 is on camera: the picture is generated without speech, and the laugh is laid to her mouth, picture-led ±2; if it won't sit, do a lip-sync pass with the same consented recording. In the B04 and B08 fallback flips her face shows for under a second, so keep the laugh off those frames.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production with the actor cast as Venus. She is not yet cast, and she will be the one voice for Venus across V01, V02 and the pilot. Her written consent is required for V01, V02 (organic and paid social, and the pitch-deck embed) and the pilot: all media, worldwide, with the term from first use set by the producer. The consent must allow takes to be edited and resequenced, and must exclude synthetic cloning or model training without separate written consent. No library or AI-generated laugh. Status: required, pending. Owner: producer.

cues.type: music: none (by design), plus the sound arc
cues.description: No score and no temp track in any cut of V01 (route R2; tone: music; taste note: sound design before music). The wind, her laugh and the room carry it. Native audio on every generated clip is muted, and no generated audio is used. The arc: the loudest point is 15.0-18.0 s, the scrub-hills roar on the third jump cut (REC 00:52:30, SND-V01-003), with the timer near the hour and her joy at its height. The big drop comes at 34.4 s, when she lowers the phone and we hear the world as it is. The quietest living moment is 45.5-50.0 s, the eyes, where the missing laugh does the telling. Digital silence runs 88.0-90.0 s under the title.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: None required while no music is used. No temp track may be cut in, even for internal use. Any track proposed later needs its own cue with a source and scope; a commercial track needs sync rights to all the publishing plus the master. Generated audio is excluded because it carries no promise of ownership or exclusivity.

cues.timing: V02-B01, 0.0-1.5 s (f0-f36); cut from V01 6.5-8.0 s; hook sync at 1.1 s (f26)
cues.description: Re-cut from the V01-B02 recordings, cut in at V01 6.5 s so every hit keeps V01's action timing. From frame 1: the engine idling and, because the driving wind is gone at the stop, the V02 script's 'wind on the mic' played as a light desert breeze bumping the mic (a separate take from the same stop-sign session). The last fingertip stroke on his black cotton shirt at 0.1 s (f2; V01 6.6 s). The collar pressed flat at 1.1 s (f26; V01 7.6 s): the hook's sync sound, inside 1.5 s. Picture-led, ±2 frames. More strokes would need a named internal jump cut; none is used. Fallback (her hand only rests on his collar): cut in at V01 5.7 s, so the single fabric touch (V01 5.8 s) lands at 0.1 s (f2) as the hook.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: production-owned recordings (SND-V01-001 and 002 sessions); scope as SND-V01-001, which names V02's organic and paid social use and the pitch-deck embed, worldwide. The library sign creak is not used in V02. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Hard cut at 1.5 (f36) to the shot at REC 00:52:30: V01-B03's third jump cut (the scrub hills; the V02 script calls the background open desert, so the editor should confirm it is the same shot). Its wind roar comes with it, limiter clamping hard: the loudest point in V02. The snatch of her laugh that lands on that cut in V01 lands here at 1.5 (SND-V02-005). No whoosh on the cut: the roar is the cut. Hard out at 4.0 (f96).
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: production-owned recording (SND-V01-003 session); scope as SND-V02-001. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Hard cut at 4.0 (f96), cut in at V01 42.8 s. The wind is gone: tyres on grit and the engine, low, heard from outside the car. The arm of the sunglasses scratches out of his hair at 4.2 s (f101; V01 43.0). His cheek leaves the leather headrest with a short creak at 5.8 s (f139; V01 44.6). No laugh. Picture-led, ±2 frames. Out at V01 44.8, before the eyes, so the eyes land in the phone frame at 6.0.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: production-owned recordings (SND-V01-006 and 007 sessions); scope as SND-V02-001. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.timing: V02-B04 to B06, 6.0-13.0 s (f144-f312); ends on the mic cut at 13.0 s (f312)
cues.description: One take, one bed. Hard cut at 6.0 (f144) back into the phone. From here the dusk wind on the mic runs continuously to 13.0, lower than in B02, because the timer runs unbroken (01:04:55, 01:04:58, 01:05:00). In B04 there is nothing else: no breath, drone or sting on his eyes. 6.0-9.1 is V02's quietest stretch before the final silence. The laugh (SND-V02-005) and the thumb (SND-V02-006) sit on top of it, and the mic cut at 13.0 (f312) ends it on the frame where the screen goes black. Flag to the editor and the generation supervisor (see blockers): this needs 7.0 s of continuous phone-frame footage, but V01-B08 has only 4.4 s (51.6-56.0 s), with the laugh 0.8 s after the frame narrows. These hits are written for a take of 7.0 s or more with V02's timing (eyes still for 3.1 s, laugh at +3.1, thumb on at +5.2, back at +6.4). If V02 is cut from V01's 4.4 s instead, SND-V02-004 to 006 get re-timed from the V01 in-points.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: production-owned recording (SND-V01-008 session); scope as SND-V02-001. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: B02: the V01 snatch, loud on the mic, on the cut. B05: soft and close, starting on the first shake of the frame (9.1, f218, picture-led, ±2) and running while his open eyes stay centred, over the SND-V02-004 bed. Off-mouth, because she is behind the phone. Same performer and the same session as SND-V01-015, with the same read: delight aimed at him, never a villain's laugh. V02 plays muted in feeds, so the shaking frame has to carry this beat on its own; with sound on, the laugh sets the irony against his eyes.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: the consented recording in SND-V01-015. The Venus actor's written consent must name V02's organic and paid social use and the pitch-deck embed, worldwide, with the term from first use. Status: required, pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: On top of the SND-V02-004 bed. Her thumb squeaks onto the flip icon from 11.2 to 11.6 (f269-f278), rests over his eyes, and slides back off from 12.4 to 12.8 (f298-f307). These are the V01-B08 thumb takes, with the same 0.4 s on, 0.8 s rest and 0.4 s back. Picture-led, ±2 frames. At 13.0 (f312) the mic cuts out on the same frame as the cut to black: a hard digital cut, with no stop chime and no UI sound. Fallback (the under-a-second flip): 2-frame dropouts at the flip and the flip back.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: production-owned phone foley (SND-V01-004 and 008 sessions). No manufacturer UI sound (A10); scope as SND-V02-001. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.description: Digital silence under the LIMERENCE card, from f312 to the last frame. No sting and no tail: the recording stopping is the sound. Sound-led, ±2 frames.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: None required, because no audio is used. At conform, check that nothing runs past f312.

cues.type: music: none (by design), plus the sound arc
cues.description: No music and no temp track, as in SND-V01-016. V02 must read with the sound off: the timer, the eyes, the thumb and the card carry it. Native audio on the generated clips is muted. The arc: the first sync sound is the fingertip stroke at 0.1 s (f2), and the hook sync is the collar press at 1.1 s (f26). The loudest point is the hard cut to the scrub-hills roar at 1.5 s (f36). The quietest stretch before the end is 6.0-9.1 s, the eyes with only dusk wind. Then the laugh against the eyes at 9.1, and digital silence from 13.0.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: None required while no music is used. No platform trending audio or library track may be added at posting; any added sound needs its own cue, source and scope. Owner for posting: producer.

cues.type: foley + atmos + production dialogue (decorum at the bar)
cues.timing: Pilot SC05-SC08, about 180-660 s (3:00-11:00); 'Have we met before?' at the top of SC05 (about 180 s); the first verdict inside SC06 (about 330-480 s); picture-led
cues.description: You hear the game on the counter; nothing scores it. Following A08, no jukebox or bar music plays. VENUS: "Have we met before?" opens it over the bare room. A straw laid flat in the wet ring makes a soft, tacky tick. A straw drawn back out makes a dry slide. A glass is set down for every drink, so each lost straw has its own sound. The first verdict (SC06): after JEAN: "She left. Packed while I was at work. I never once raised my voice." her glass goes down, then the dry slide of the wall straw, then JEAN: "That's a no?" VENUS: "That's a drink." In SC07 the chimney straw makes a faint waxy drag as it is pushed into the soft candle wax. The room is a near-empty Thursday bar, carried by a drinks-fridge compressor and a glass washer; any background voices are unintelligible walla. Dialogue is recorded clean on set, with nothing under it but the room. Cut on the laughs (tone: genuine).
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production, and production dialogue recorded on set with the Venus, Jean and Bartender actors, whose written consent for the pilot scope is required. Walla is recorded with consented background performers and kept unintelligible; any intelligible speech needs consent as dialogue. Scope: the pilot, as SND-D01-001. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.type: foley (the tin and the last straw)
cues.timing: Pilot SC12-SC13, about 900-1200 s (15:00-20:00); the lid opens at the end of SC13, about 1195 s, the Act Two button; picture-led
cues.description: No music in either scene (A08). SC12: her glass set down on the white lacquered table, the straw standing in its ice. The closed metal tin slides across to him in one continuous glide of metal on lacquer, a low even hiss with no stutter. He turns it over in his palm; nothing inside is heard. He tries the lid: it lifts a hair and clicks back shut under her fingertip, one dry metal click. Then VENUS: "Let's take a trip." Through both scenes the ice settles in her glass around the standing straw, a soft shift now and then between lines, never under a word. SC13: after JEAN: "That's for you to find out." the straw is drawn out of the ice with a wet drag and laid flat on the table with a wet tick. Her fingertip lifts, the hinged lid's catch releases, and the lid swings open toward him: a dry hinge, and a small knock as it meets its stop. Hard cut on the knock: the Act Two out. Nothing inside the tin is heard, now or later, because the method stays off screen.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production (a prop tin with a hinged lid, a white lacquered table, glass, ice, straw). The dialogue is covered by the Venus and Jean actors' written consent for the pilot. Scope: the pilot, as SND-D01-001; owned by the production. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.timing: Pilot SC15, about 1290-1440 s (21:30-24:00); the rasp about 1400 s, before the track enters; picture-led
cues.description: His breathing is Jean's last sound: slow and loud, face-down, muffled by the pillow. Her side of the room: his black clothes folded square (cotton on cotton), the magnetic catch of the mirror cabinet, and one lid of the pill organiser snapped open and shut, with the tablets shifting once. No label is read and no drug is named. Back in bed, his breathing stops for a long gap, 6-8 s of room tone with nothing in it, then catches with one rasp on the inhale (about 1400 s). No gurgle and no death-rattle cliché. This silence is the quietest point of the night. Then comes the track (SND-D01-001), put on low, and he breathes on in its holes. The speaker's volume button takes three soft presses, each a step louder, until the holes no longer let his breathing through.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: recorded for this production with the actor cast as Jean (not yet cast). His written consent is required for his breathing and the rasp in the pilot's scope (as SND-D01-001). No library or synthetic breath. The foley is owned by the production. Status: required, pending. Owner: producer.

cues.timing: Pilot SC15-SC16: entry about 1410 s (23:30), after the rasp in SND-D01-002; exit at her switch-off, about 1525 s (25:25); the line in a bar-4 hole inside SC16 (1440-1530 s); picture-led, moves with the pilot edit
cues.description: The pilot's only music (A08). Venus plays it from the small white speaker on the nightstand to quiet herself; it is never score. Perspective: heard from the bed, from a small mono speaker that plays little below about 120 Hz. Brief for the composer: 100 BPM in 4/4 (beat 0.6 s, bar 2.4 s), one four-bar loop of 9.6 s that loops with no click, gap or tail at the join from bar 4 back to bar 1. It is written for the speaker's range. Bars 1-3 have a soft four-on-the-floor kick whose attack carries the pulse, an off-beat bass line pitched so its upper harmonics carry, electric-piano minor-ninth chords, a filtered pad and a low, wordless female vocal. Bar 4 (7.2-9.6 s of each loop) is the hole: kick, bass and electric piano all drop out, leaving only the pad, with its filter closed down, and one held low vocal note, so 1-4 kHz is nearly empty for 2.4 s. Entry: a click on the speaker's play button, with the loop starting low on a bar-1 downbeat. SC15: at low volume his breathing comes through each hole; she turns it up (the three presses in SND-D01-002) until the pad and the held note cover it. SC16: the same four bars come round, and now each hole carries no breath. VENUS: "J. Stay for breakfast." sits in one hole: 4 words in about 1.6 s of its 2.4 s. Read: said to him, landing on "Stay"; she is coaxing him up; not a plea, not grief. The music is laid in post, not played back on set, so the line records clean. Exit: she switches it off. The button clicks, the track stops hard mid-bar with no ring-out, and the room is silent. Swap test: the hole is built for his breath, so on another film it lands on nothing.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: commissioned original composition and master, with a wordless session vocalist. Scope: the pilot episode in all media, worldwide, in perpetuity, plus trailer, pitch and promo use of the pilot. Required: the composer's originality warranty and a similarity check, plus the vocalist's written consent for that scope. No generated vocals or stems. The line is covered by the Venus actor's consent (SND-V01-015). Status: pending. Owner: producer. Not used in V01 or V02.

cues.timing: Pilot SC17, about 1530-1680 s (25:30-28:00); starts in the silence after the switch-off in SND-D01-001; picture-led
cues.description: No music: the switch-off at the end of SC16 left the room silent, and it stays silent apart from her work. Room tone: sealed and white, with a faint hiss from an air vent. Absent: the street, the neighbours and any clock, because the windows are shut and nothing in the room is allowed to move. Dressing him: black cotton drawn over his arms, the white armchair's cushion sighing under his weight, and the acetate hinge of his sunglasses opened and slid on (the V01 acetate take, a plant for SC01). The bed: the old sheets dragged off, the fitted sheet's elastic snapping off each corner, one fresh sheet snapped open in the air, four corners pulled tight and tucked, her palms smoothing. The threshold: her knees on the hard floor, the damp cloth scrubbing the three drops in short hard strokes, two soft folds as the pink cloth goes square, then the bin's pedal and lid. The tin's hinge and a click as it shuts; fabric as it goes into her pocket with the flat straw. Then the hold on the finished room, with Jean in the white chair: room tone only, longer than is comfortable (tone: clean). Jean makes no sound.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production, with the sunglasses from the V01 acetate session and room tone recorded in a white-finished interior (location release required). Scope: the pilot, as SND-D01-001; owned by the production. Status: pending. Owner: producer.

cues.type: foley + sfx (the tag: the flip-camera press)
cues.timing: Pilot SC18, about 1680-1800 s (28:00-30:00); the flip-camera press about 1750 s; picture-led
cues.description: This continues from V01, with the same motel room tone and wind (SND-V01-012 and 013). An acetate tick as she sets his sunglasses down by the oranges. Two push pins pressed into the wall for the new man's prints. Cotton as her head settles on his shoulder, and the phone lifted. The focal sound, ahead of the printer: her thumb squeaks across the glass to the flip-camera icon and makes the small knock in the phone body. These are the same foley takes as SND-V01-004 and 008, reused on purpose so the ear knows the gesture. This time there is no slide back: the press completes. The flip is heard as the 2-frame dropout from the V01 fallbacks: the room tone drops out for 2 frames and comes back. Two fingers turn his chin; his collar shifts and his chair creaks. The photo is taken with no shutter sound (original UI, A10). Then the palm-sized printer: a motor whir and the paper feeding out, the only mechanical sound in a silent room. One more pin as the photo goes up, then room tone and wind, echoing V01's held frame. Proposal, for approval: no laugh here. Every laugh so far was aimed at him from behind the lens; in front of it she only smiles, and the room stays quiet.
cues.licensing_or_consent_requirement: Source: foley recorded for this production, with the thumb takes reused from the SND-V01-004 and 008 sessions, the printer recorded on a debadged unit and the room tone reused from the V01 session. Scope: the pilot, as SND-D01-001; owned by the production. No manufacturer UI sounds (A10). Status: pending. Owner: producer.

assumptions: All timings are seconds from the first frame of each deliverable at 24 fps, with frame = round(s x 24). No picture exists yet, so every sync point is a target at ±2 frames, picture-led unless the cue marks it sound-led.
V01 and V02 have no spoken lines (A15). Venus's laugh is the only voice, and Jean makes no sound in either, not even breath.
Native audio on every generated clip is muted, and no generated audio is used anywhere.
The picture car is generated. Its sound is recorded on a hired vintage open two-seater. That such a car can be hired is a hypothesis, and no make is identified.

V02's sound is re-cut from V01's recordings on V02's own beats, and each shot's V01 in-point is stated: B01 at 6.5 s, B02 at 15.0 s, B03 at 42.8 s. B04 to B06 assume a continuous phone-frame take of at least 7.0 s, which is flagged in blockers.
V02-B02's REC 00:52:30 shot is V01-B03's third jump cut, which V01's picture calls scrub hills and V02's calls open desert. The sound follows the shot, and the editor confirms it is the same one.
The V02-B01 script says 'wind on the mic', but the driving wind is gone at the stop sign (V01-B02). It is played as a light breeze bumping the mic, taken from the same stop-sign session.

The D01 cues are pilot anchors (decorum, the tin, Jean's breathing, the track, the clean-up, the tag), not full coverage. Their times come from the outline's scene times and will move with the pilot edit.
100 BPM, the four-bar loop and the bar-4 hole are a proposal for the commission, not a spec from Lucas. The 2.4 s hole is sized to hold one slow exhale; this is a design intent, not a measured fact.
The track is commissioned full-range. The small mono speaker perspective (little below about 120 Hz) is how it is heard in the scene; its treatment belongs to the mix.
The tin has a hinged lid; this is a prop choice for production design to confirm. Nothing inside the tin is ever heard, so the method stays off screen (must avoid).
Loudness targets and delivery specs are left to the mix, so none are stated here.
The Venus, Jean and Bartender actors are not yet cast, so every voice consent stays pending until they are.
Gun-handling foley is recorded with a non-firing replica; production safety to confirm.

The 2-frame audio dropout at the front-camera flip is a design choice, not a claim about how any phone behaves. In the tag it is used on purpose in the room's perspective, the one time the room is heard the way the phone hears it.
The tag with no laugh is a proposal marked for approval; the script has her smiling, not laughing.

Taste notes followed: sound design before music (no score in V01 or V02, and the pilot's only music plays inside the scene); restraint over explanation (no stings or drones on the eyes, the gun, the tin or the title); hands before faces (hand foley leads every beat); dry over sentimental (the verdict heard as a glass set down). None is broken on purpose.

blockers.issue: V02-B04 to B06 (6.0-13.0 s) run on one unbroken timer (01:04:55, 01:04:58, 01:05:00), so they need 7.0 s of continuous phone-frame footage of Jean's open eyes, with V02's action timing: still for 3.1 s, laugh at +3.1 s, thumb on at +5.2 s, thumb back at +6.4 s. V01-B08 has only 4.4 s of phone-frame footage (51.6-56.0 s), and its laugh comes 0.8 s after the frame narrows, so V01's cut cannot supply it.
blockers.resolution: Either generate the phone-frame eyes take at 7.0 s or longer with V02's action timing (SND-V02-004 to 006 are written for this), or re-time V02-B04 to B06 from V01's 4.4 s. If it is re-timed, the sound designer re-times SND-V02-004 to 006 from the V01 in-points.

evidence.specificity: All six earlier notes have been fixed. The V02 hits are now worked out from V01 in-points: "cut in at V01 6.5 s so every hit keeps V01's action timing... The collar pressed flat at 1.1 s (f26; V01 7.6 s)" and "The arm of the sunglasses scratches out of his hair at 4.2 s (f101; V01 43.0)". I checked every frame number against round(s x 24) and all are correct. The cues name the thing that makes each sound and the order it happens in, for example "The lantern's plastic switch clicks at 72.4 (f1738), two frames before the light comes up (f1740)" and "The glovebox push-button latch releases and the lid drops onto its stays at 57.4 (f1378)". The music brief is something a composer can build from: "100 BPM in 4/4 (beat 0.6 s, bar 2.4 s), one four-bar loop of 9.6 s that loops with no click, gap or tail at the join from bar 4 back to bar 1." The storyboard and the editor could act on this without asking a question.
evidence.distinctiveness: The route's gesture is carried by sound across the whole pilot: "These are the same foley takes as SND-V01-004 and 008, reused on purpose so the ear knows the gesture. This time there is no slide back: the press completes." The diegetic track is written for this one scene: "Swap test: the hole is built for his breath, so on another film it lands on nothing." There are details nobody else would think of: "the pistol's steel knocks the glovebox floor once... No slide rack, no hammer click and no metal sting: the gun is carried, not introduced", and the proposal to leave out the laugh: "Every laugh so far was aimed at him from behind the lens; in front of it she only smiles." Dropped into another film, these cues land on nothing.
evidence.fit: The new D01-005 and D01-006 now cover the tin must-include and the bed remake. D01-005 adds "it lifts a hair and clicks back shut under her fingertip", then the straw is laid flat, and only after that "the lid swings open toward him... Hard cut on the knock: the Act Two out." D01-006 adds "one fresh sheet snapped open in the air, four corners pulled tight and tucked". The must-avoids are kept: "Nothing inside the tin is heard, now or later, because the method stays off screen", and for the meds, "one lid of the pill organiser snapped open and shut, with the tablets shifting once. No label is read and no drug is named." It follows route R2's sound rule to the letter: phone-mic wind and her laugh, a perspective drop when she lowers the phone, no score in V01 or V02, and "Digital silence runs 88.0-90.0 s under the title." Laugh consent "must exclude synthetic cloning or model training". There are no brands and no voiceover. The one small gap is the bar walla, which blurs Venus's "empty bar" line.
evidence.craft: The craft notes from the last round are fixed. "seamlessly" is gone. The speaker's range now drives the arrangement: "a small mono speaker that plays little below about 120 Hz... Bar 4 (7.2-9.6 s of each loop) is the hole: kick, bass and electric piano all drop out, leaving only the pad, with its filter closed down." V02-B04 to B06 is one bed now ("6.0-13.0... one take, one bed"), and the 7.0 s footage gap is logged as a blocker with owners. Library rights now name territory and term: "all media, worldwide, term from first use in perpetuity (or the term the producer sets)". The hair flutter and the candle, which nothing could make heard, are gone. Every right is left pending with the producer. It isn't a 9 yet because a few logic slips remain. "Sound-led: the picture stays still and nothing needs to hit these knocks" contradicts the brief's definition of sound-led. A swollen door that "scrapes open over grit" is then heard with "its latch knocks in the keeper". "A fingertip taps the glass at 27.0" is an action the phone-screen picture never shows. In SC16, "each hole carries no breath" comes at a level that has already covered his breathing, so nobody can hear that the breath is missing.

notes.target: SND-D01-001 and SND-D01-002 (SC16): the hole that 'carries no breath'
notes.note: In SC15 she turns the track up "until the pad and the held note cover it". In SC16 the loop is still playing at that level, so an empty hole tells the listener nothing: a breath would have been covered anyway. Name the SC16 perspective so the missing breath can be heard. Put the listener on her pillow, facing him, a hand-width from his open mouth, with the speaker across the bed behind her. At that distance a breath would sit clearly in the 1-4 kHz hole even at the volume she left it. Write down that the SC15 covering was heard from her side, turned away from him. Give one full loop (9.6 s, holes at +7.2 and +16.8 s) with nothing in the hole before "J. Stay for breakfast.", so the empty hole plays twice before she speaks.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Name the source, action, material and perspective'; 'If a cue would fit another film unchanged, it is not finished.' Quality bar, craft: 'nothing physically implausible'. Must-include: the morning after, 'waiting for him to turn over'.

notes.target: SND-V01-005 (V01-B05, 27.0 s): the fingertip tap that turns on the video light
notes.note: Under R2 the picture is her phone's screen, and her thumb on the glass is visible in B04 and B08. A tap on the glass at 27.0 with no finger in the picture breaks that rule. Change the cause to a side-button press on the phone body. It sits off the screen, so it can be heard without being seen: a small plastic click heard through the chassis, with a touch of handling noise. Keep it at 27.0 (f648), two frames before the light (f650). If the glass tap stays, flag it to the storyboard and the generation supervisor: her fingertip must enter the frame at f648.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Every effect serves an action on screen or a story event off it. Cause before effect.' Route R2 visual language: 'while she films, the picture is her phone's screen'.

notes.target: SND-V01-013 (V01-B13, 82.0-88.0 s): the door latch and the 'sound-led' label
notes.note: SND-V01-011 establishes the door as swollen, shouldered open and scraping over grit. A door that tight can't rattle its latch in the keeper, and B13 is 'a held frame in which nothing moves'. Replace the knocks with what a jammed door does in a gust: a low timber creak as the door takes the pressure, and fine grit hissing against its outside face. Keep the times, 83.6 (f2006) and 86.2 (f2069), and keep the last gust gone by 87.8. Relabel the cue from 'sound-led' to 'free-running: no picture event, placed anywhere in 82.0-87.8'. The brief defines sound-led as 'picture must hit it', which this cue says it does not need.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'a sync point is... marked sound-led (picture must hit it) or picture-led'. Quality bar, craft: 'continuity that holds'. V01-B13 picture.

notes.target: SND-D01-004 (SC05-SC08): the room and the through-the-window section
notes.note: Venus's line is 'A true martyr on a Thursday night, alone in an empty bar.' Audible walla undercuts it. Commit to the empty bar: drop the walla and its consent line, and let the only other people be the bartender and the glass washer he loads. Then write what's heard in SC08, 'seen silent through the window and cut on the laughs'. Hear it from the street through plate glass: the room muffled down to its two laughs, the straws inaudible, and the street's own hum. That includes the moment her fingertip draws out the roof straw (the S03 frame). The cut lands on his laugh coming through the glass.
notes.source: Script SC06 and SC08. Tone: 'Genuine: ... cut on the laughs'. Craft brief: 'An atmosphere names what's heard, off screen too, and what's absent and why'; 'Clearly heard background speech needs consent too'.

notes.target: Small wording fixes: SND-V01-004, SND-V01-006, SND-V02-001
notes.note: SND-V01-004: 'a little less roar now that the sun is lower' gives the wrong cause. The sun doesn't change wind roar; say the car has slowed. SND-V01-006: 'Absent: birds, insects and any other engine' needs its reason. Say it's a design choice that keeps the world empty around the two of them, not a claim about the desert. SND-V02-001: the rights line says SND-V01-001 'names V02's organic and paid social use', but 001 says 'all media'. Make the cross-reference match 001's wording.
notes.source: Craft brief: 'Cause before effect'; 'what's absent and why'. Quality bar, craft: 'every cross-reference to another department's IDs is right'.

keep: V02 hits worked out from stated V01 in-points (6.5, 15.0 and 42.8 s), with the 7.0 s continuous phone-frame take logged as a blocker with owners
One continuous dusk-wind bed across V02-B04 to B06, ended by the mic cut on the frame that goes black (f312)

The tag (SND-D01-003): the same thumb foley takes reused on purpose, no slide back, the 2-frame dropout for the flip, no shutter sound, the printer whir as the only mechanical sound, and the no-laugh proposal marked for approval

The trance-soul commission: 100 BPM, a 9.6 s four-bar loop with no click at the join, the bar-4 hole built for a small mono speaker, entry after the rasp, 'J. Stay for breakfast.' placed in a hole, and a hard mid-bar stop when she switches it off

The laugh as Venus's only voice in V01 and V02, with read notes ('delight, not mania... never a villain's laugh'), one performer throughout, and consent that excludes cloning; Jean silent everywhere, not even breath
No score in V01 or V02, no stings on the eyes, the gun, the tin or the title, and a hard cut to digital silence at f2112 and f312

direction.note: Shoot it in a 35mm film style. Every shot reads as 35mm motion-picture film: fine visible grain, soft halation around highlights and practicals, film colour with gentle highlight roll-off and deep but not crushed blacks, and the depth of field and perspective of 35mm-format lenses. Keep the look consistent across every deliverable, the 9:16 cut-down and the stills included, and say how. Footage the audience sees on Venus's phone screen is in-world phone video: decide on purpose whether it stays phone video or is shown as film, and say why.
direction.lucas_words: I would for it be shot in 35mm film style
